definition_zh: 获胜者；得奖者；成功的事物
definition_en: the person or team that comes first in a contest, or a thing that turns out to be a great success
core_image: 领奖台上最高的那一级，那个人低头去接挂上来的奖牌
scene: 颁奖时，最高的那一级台阶上，那个人低头让奖牌挂上脖子，手还在微微发抖。 The winner of the spelling contest had never missed a single word.
sceneCN: 这里 winner 是「获胜者」（第 1 个义项：比赛中拿到第一名的人）；句意为拼写比赛的获胜者一个词都没写错。领奖台上低头接奖牌的那一刻，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 获胜者；得奖者；成功之作

senses.title: The one who comes first
senses.definition: the person or team that finishes ahead of all others in a game or race
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛或竞赛中领先所有人的个人或队伍
senses.example: The winner of the spelling contest had never missed a single word.
senses.exampleCN: 拼写比赛的获胜者一个词都没写错。
senses.why: The ending -er names the doer, so the winner is simply the one who wins.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -er 命名做事的人，所以 winner 就是那个 win 的人。

senses.title: A person given a prize
senses.definition: a person who receives an award for a work, a piece of writing or a performance
senses.definitionCN: 因作品、文章或表演而获得奖项的人
senses.example: The winner of the essay prize was a girl of fifteen.
senses.exampleCN: 作文奖的得主是一个十五岁的女孩。
senses.why: Not every award comes from a fight, yet the person chosen is still the one who came out on top.
senses.whyCN: 并非每个奖项都来自搏斗，但被选中的人依然是那个拔尖的人。

senses.title: A thing that succeeds
senses.definition: a product, idea or plan that turns out to be very successful
senses.definitionCN: 结果非常成功的产品、想法或方案
senses.example: The new bus service was an immediate winner with commuters.
senses.exampleCN: 新的公交线路立刻受到通勤者的欢迎。
senses.why: People carried the word from persons to things, saying a product won its market just as a runner wins a race.
senses.whyCN: 人们把这个词从人搬到物上，说一个产品赢下了市场，正如跑者赢下比赛。

intro.en: Winner is win plus the doer ending -er, and the base goes back to Old English winnan, to labour and fight.
intro.cn: winner 是 win 加上表施动者的词尾 -er，而词根可回到古英语 winnan（劳作、争斗）。

items.en: winnan meant to struggle and toil, so a winner was first a person who had fought hard.
items.cn: winnan 表示奋斗与劳作，所以 winner 起初指奋力争斗过的人。

items.en: The agent ending -a formed names such as winnend, one who wins.
items.cn: 施动词尾 -a 造出 winnend 之类的名字，意为赢的人。

items.en: The ending became -ere, giving winner, and victory in games came to the front.
items.cn: 词尾变为 -ere，形成 winner，游戏中的取胜义走到了前面。

items.en: Sports reporting fixed the word for the first-place person or team.
items.cn: 体育报道把这个词固定给第一名的个人或队伍。

items.en: Advertisers extended it to products and ideas, so a bus route could be a winner too.
items.cn: 广告人又把它扩展到产品与想法，于是一条公交线路也能是赢家。

note.en: The first group collects members of the same family, the second other names for the person who comes first.
note.cn: 第一组收同族成员，第二组收其他指第一名的称呼。

entries.definition: The verb behind the person.
Money gained from a bet or a game.
The coldest of the seasons.
Belonging to the winner in a possessive form.
The overall best in a sport, often holding a title.
A formal word for the one who defeats another.
The one who comes last instead of first.

normalIntro.en: Winner is one of the easiest family members: win plus the -er that means the person who does it.
normalIntro.cn: winner 是最容易记的词族成员之一：win 加上表示「做此事的人」的 -er。

normal.en: Win plus er, the same -er as in teacher and worker.
normal.cn: win 加 er，与 teacher、worker 里的 -er 一样。

normal.en: Double n is kept from win before the ending.
normal.cn: 加词尾前保留了 win 的两个 n。

normal.en: The -ner ending sounds like the last syllable of dinner, a prize meal.
normal.cn: 结尾的 -ner 听起来像 dinner 的末音节，像一顿庆功饭。

normal.en: Winnings is the money, winner is the person: one letter more, one meaning more.
normal.cn: winnings 是钱，winner 是人：多一个字母，多一层意思。

normal.en: A winner is not always first; sometimes it is the product everyone buys.
normal.cn: winner 不一定永远是第一名，有时是人人都在买的产品。

abstract.en: A medal lowered over a bowed head.
abstract.cn: 奖牌从上方挂向低下的头。

abstract.en: A name called out and a silence just after it.
abstract.cn: 名字被念出来之后那一小段安静。

abstract.en: The feeling inside a hand that will not stop shaking.
abstract.cn: 一只停不下颤抖的手里的感受。

examples.en: The winner received a cup and a small cheque.
examples.cn: 获胜者得到一只奖杯和一张小支票。

examples.en: Nobody was surprised when she was announced as the winner.
examples.cn: 宣布她是获胜者时，没人感到惊讶。

examples.en: The design was a winner from the first day in the shops.
examples.cn: 这个设计从上市第一天起就是赢家。

dict_mnemonic.text: win（赢）+ er（人）—— 赢的那个人，就是「获胜者」。

root: 古英语 winnan（奋斗、争得）→ win → win + -er → winner；同族有 winning、winnings、win。

sensesIntro.en: A hard fighter becomes the first-place person, then the receiver of a prize, and finally any thing that succeeds.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个奋力争斗的人，先成为第一名，再成为领奖的人，最后成了任何成功的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the highest step of the platform, a bowed head.
core.cn: 核心意象：领奖台最高的那一级，低下去的头。

branches.en: The contest branch: a spelling champion with no mistakes.
branches.cn: 竞赛分支：一个错字都没有的拼写冠军。

branches.en: The award branch: a fifteen-year-old essay winner.
branches.cn: 奖项分支：一个十五岁的作文奖得主。

branches.en: The product branch: a bus route that commuters love.
branches.cn: 产品分支：通勤者喜爱的公交线路。

branches.en: The person branch: the doer of the verb, now wearing a medal.
branches.cn: 人物分支：动词的施动者，如今挂着奖牌。

branches.en: The evaluation branch: a winner is whatever others decide to honour.
branches.cn: 评价分支：赢家是别人决定要表彰的那一个。

intro.en: Winner is a transparent piece of word building: the root win plus the agent suffix -er.
intro.cn: winner 是构造极透明的词：词根 win 加上施动词尾 -er。

latinIntro.en: Neither the root nor the suffix is Latin here; the Latin entry is only a borrowed synonym.
latinIntro.cn: 这里的词根与词尾都不是拉丁语；拉丁条目只是借入的同义词。

items.exampleCN: 它构成 winners 与 winnings。

items.meaning: the one who does not win
items.exampleCN: 同一构词法用在 lose 上。
这个词进入了经济领域。

definition_zh: 毯子；覆盖层；全面的
definition_en: a thick cover used to keep warm in bed
core_image: 沙发上叠得厚厚的毛毯
scene: 沙发上叠着一条厚厚的毛毯。 She pulled the blanket up to her chin.
sceneCN: 这里 blanket 是「毯子」（第 1 个义项：保暖的厚覆盖物）；句意是她把毯子拉到下巴。

derivatives.zh: 被覆盖住的，常指被雪或雾盖住
语义关联词，义为「被子」，与 blanket 同属床上覆盖物

senses.title: A thick warm bed cover
senses.definition: a thick cover made of wool or similar material for warmth
senses.definitionCN: 用羊毛或类似材料制成、用于保暖的厚覆盖物
senses.example: She pulled the blanket up to her chin.
senses.exampleCN: 她把毯子拉到下巴。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, a cloth spread over a sleeper.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，一块盖在睡觉者身上的布。

senses.title: A thick covering layer
senses.definition: a thick layer that covers something completely
senses.definitionCN: 把某物完全盖住的厚厚一层
senses.example: A blanket of snow covered the field.
senses.exampleCN: 一层积雪盖住了田野。
senses.why: Snow spread like cloth over the ground, so the cover word extended.
senses.whyCN: 积雪像布一样铺在地上，覆盖物这个词就扩展开来。

senses.title: Applying to everything
senses.definition: affecting all cases or people without exception
senses.definitionCN: 无一例外地影响所有情况或所有人
senses.example: The city issued a blanket ban on smoking.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市发布了全面禁烟令。
senses.why: A cover over everything became an image for a rule over everything.
senses.whyCN: 盖住一切的布，成了覆盖一切的规定这一意象。

intro.en: Blanket began as a white woollen cloth and then covered anything.
intro.cn: blanket 本指一种白色毛布，后来覆盖到了一切事物上。

items.en: blanchet named a white woollen cloth.
items.cn: blanchet 指一种白色毛布。

items.en: blanket became a cover for a bed.
items.cn: blanket 成为床上的覆盖物。

items.en: blanket also meant any thick covering.
items.cn: blanket 也可指任何厚厚的覆盖层。

items.en: blanket began to mean covering all cases.
items.cn: blanket 开始表示涵盖所有情况。

items.en: blanket is both a cover and a total measure.
items.cn: 如今 blanket 既是覆盖物，也是全面措施。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the blan- opening; the near-meaning group names bedding and covers.
note.cn: 形近组都以 blan- 开头；近义组是床上用品与覆盖物。

entries.definition: empty, with nothing written
a support fixed to a wall
a light that flashes on and off
a padded cover for a bed
a small light blanket
something placed over another thing

normalIntro.en: A blanket is cloth spread over you, and later anything spread over a whole area.
normalIntro.cn: blanket 是盖在身上的布，后来也指铺满整个区域的东西。

normal.en: A blanket of snow uses the covering sense.
normal.cn: a blanket of snow 用的是覆盖层义。

normal.en: Blanket ban means a ban with no exceptions.
normal.cn: blanket ban 指没有例外的禁令。

normal.en: Electric blanket has heating wires inside.
normal.cn: electric blanket 里有电热丝。

normal.en: The plural simply adds s.
normal.cn: 复数直接加 s。

normal.en: Blanket and blank share the same opening.
normal.cn: blanket 与 blank 开头相同。

abstract.en: See a folded wool blanket on a sofa.
abstract.cn: 想象沙发上叠着一条羊毛毯。

abstract.en: See snow hiding a whole field.
abstract.cn: 想象大雪盖住整片田野。

abstract.en: See one rule posted on every door.
abstract.cn: 想象每扇门上都贴着同一条规定。

examples.en: She pulled the blanket up to her chin.
examples.cn: 她把毯子拉到下巴。

examples.en: A blanket of snow covered the field.
examples.cn: 一层积雪盖住了田野。

examples.en: The city issued a blanket ban on smoking.
examples.cn: 这座城市发布了全面禁烟令。

dict_mnemonic.text: blanket 来自表示白色的词，原指白色毛布，后来不管什么颜色，只要是厚毯子都叫 blanket。

root: blanket 源自古法语 blanchet，本指白色毛布，词根与 blanc（白）相关；中古英语指床上的毯子，后引申为厚覆盖层与「全面」的形容词义。

sensesIntro.en: A cloth over a sleeper, a layer over a field, a rule over everyone.
sensesIntro.cn: 盖在睡者身上的布、铺在田野上的层、加在所有人身上的规定。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick woollen blanket folded on a sofa.
core.cn: 核心意象：沙发上叠好的厚毛毯。

branches.en: a warm blanket
branches.cn: 温暖的毯子

branches.en: an electric blanket
branches.cn: 电热毯

branches.en: a blanket of snow
branches.cn: 一层积雪

branches.en: a blanket ban
branches.cn: 全面禁令

branches.en: blanket coverage
branches.cn: 全面覆盖

intro.en: Blanket is a noun that also works as an adjective before words like ban.
intro.cn: blanket 是名词，也可放在 ban 一类词前作形容词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Germanic and reached English through French.
latinIntro.cn: 词基属日耳曼语，经法语传入英语。

definition_zh: 重新开始；恢复；重新取得
definition_en: to begin again after a pause, or to take back a position
core_image: 停下的钟摆被人轻轻一推，又重新摆动起来
scene: 雨停之后，工人们重新开始修建那条小路。 After the rain stopped, the workers resumed building the path.
sceneCN: 这里 resume 是「重新开始」（第 1 个义项：停顿之后再次进行）；句意：雨停之后，工人们重新开始修建那条小路。

pos.zh: 重新开始；恢复；重新取得

senses.title: Begin again
senses.definition: to start something again after a break
senses.definitionCN: 在停顿之后再次开始某事
senses.example: The meeting will resume after lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 会议将在午餐后重新开始。
senses.why: The Latin source means to take up again, so resuming picks an activity back up.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为重新拿起，因此 resume 就是把活动重新拾起。

senses.title: Take back a position
senses.definition: to return to an office, seat or duty
senses.definitionCN: 回到职位、座位或职责上
senses.example: She resumed her duties as manager in May.
senses.exampleCN: 她在五月重新履行经理职责。
senses.why: Taking up a role again is the same gesture of picking something back up.
senses.whyCN: 重新担任职务，同样是「重新拿起」的动作。

intro.en: Resume comes from Latin resumere, to take up again, from sumere, to take.
intro.cn: resume 源自拉丁语 resumere（重新拿起），由 sumere（拿）构成。

items.en: Sumere means to take up.
items.cn: sumere 意为拿起。

items.en: Resumere means to take up again.
items.cn: resumere 意为重新拿起。

items.en: Resumer keeps the sense of continuing.
items.cn: resumer 保留了继续的含义。

items.en: Resume means begin again after stopping.
items.cn: resume 意为停下后重新开始。

items.en: It also means return to an office or duty.
items.cn: 它也指回到职位或职责。

note.en: Resume is close to continue and restart, and is not the noun for a CV.
note.cn: resume 与 continue、restart 相近，注意它不是指简历的名词。

entries.definition: the act of starting again
able to be started again
to suppose something is true
to keep doing something
to begin again
to begin something again with new energy

normalIntro.en: Resume is re- plus sume, take: take the activity up again.
normalIntro.cn: resume 是 re- 加 sume（拿）：把活动重新拿起来。

normal.en: Resume work means start working again after a break.
normal.cn: resume work 意为休息后重新工作。

normal.en: Resume talks means bring the talks back to life.
normal.cn: resume talks 意为让谈判重新进行。

normal.en: Resume one's seat means sit down again.
normal.cn: resume one's seat 意为重新坐下。

normal.en: The noun resumption names the fresh start.
normal.cn: 名词 resumption 指重新开始。

normal.en: Keep resume apart from the CV spelled with accents.
normal.cn: 注意把 resume 与带重音符号的简历一词区分开。

abstract.en: Picture a paused clock starting to tick again.
abstract.cn: 想象一只停下的钟重新滴答走动。

abstract.en: Imagine a book reopened at the exact page.
abstract.cn: 想象一本书正好在原来那页重新打开。

abstract.en: Think of a runner who stumbles and then sets off again.
abstract.cn: 想象跑步者踉跄一下后又重新起跑。

examples.en: Negotiations resumed after a short pause.
examples.cn: 短暂停顿后谈判重新开始。

examples.en: He resumed his seat at the head of the table.
examples.cn: 他重新坐回桌子主位。

examples.en: The team hopes to resume training next week.
examples.cn: 球队希望下周恢复训练。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（再）＋ sume（拿起）」——把放下的事重新拿起来，就是重新开始；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（再）＋ sumere（拿）→ resumere（重新拿起）→ 法语 resumer → resume，核心义「把停下的活动重新拿起」。

sensesIntro.en: Resume first means begin again after a break, and then return to a position or duty.
sensesIntro.cn: resume 先指停顿后重新开始，再指回到职位或职责。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stopped pendulum pushed back into motion.
core.cn: 核心意象：停下的钟摆被推一下又重新摆动。

branches.en: An activity starts again after a gap.
branches.cn: 活动在间隔之后再次开始。

branches.en: A person returns to an office or duty.
branches.cn: 人回到职位或职责上。

branches.en: Returning to work is both a fresh start and a return.
branches.cn: 重返工作是重新开始，也是回归。

branches.en: Talks and work are the most common objects.
branches.cn: 谈判与工作是最常见的宾语。

branches.en: Royalty and officials also resume duties.
branches.cn: 王室成员与官员也会恢复职责。

intro.en: Resume is re- plus sumere, to take, with a French spelling in between.
intro.cn: resume 由 re- 与 sumere（拿）构成，中间经过法语拼写。

latinIntro.en: Latin sumere means to take up; resumere means to take up again.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sumere 意为拿起；resumere 意为重新拿起。

items.exampleCN: 法语 resumer 传递了该词。

items.example: Resumable describes a task that can pause and restart.
items.exampleCN: resumable 描述可暂停再继续的任务。

definition_zh: 代数；代数学；代数体系
definition_en: a branch of mathematics in which letters and symbols stand for unknown numbers
core_image: 黑板上字母代替未知数，等式像天平两边保持平衡
scene: 老师把未知数写成字母，让学生一步步解出它的值。 In algebra, letters stand for numbers we do not yet know.
sceneCN: 这里 algebra 是「代数」（第 1 个义项：用符号代替数的数学分支）；句意为在代数里，字母代表我们还不知道的数。

pos.zh: 名词：代数；代数学；代数体系

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ic 构成，义为「代数的；代数式的」
由 algebraic 加 -ly 构成，义为「用代数方法地」
由本词加 -ist 构成，义为「代数学家」

senses.title: The branch of mathematics
senses.definition: the branch of mathematics that uses letters and symbols to represent numbers and solve equations
senses.definitionCN: 用字母和符号表示数并解方程的数学分支
senses.example: She started studying algebra at the age of twelve.
senses.exampleCN: 她十二岁开始学代数。
senses.why: The Arabic name meant the reunion of broken parts, and the subject is exactly that: pieces of a problem are put back together through symbols.
senses.whyCN: 这个阿拉伯语名称意为「破碎部分的重聚」，而这门学科做的正是这件事：用符号把问题的碎片重新拼合。

senses.title: A system of symbolic rules
senses.definition: a particular system of symbols and operations, such as Boolean algebra or linear algebra
senses.definitionCN: 一套特定的符号与运算体系，如布尔代数或线性代数
senses.example: Boolean algebra uses two values, true and false.
senses.exampleCN: 布尔代数使用真与假两个值。
senses.why: Once the method exists, each set of rules can be called an algebra, the way each language has its own grammar.
senses.whyCN: 方法一旦存在，每一套规则都可以称为一种代数，就像每种语言都有自己的语法。

senses.title: Schoolwork with unknowns
senses.definition: the school activity of solving problems with unknown quantities represented by letters
senses.definitionCN: 用字母代表未知量来解题的学校课业
senses.example: He spent the evening doing algebra before the test.
senses.exampleCN: 考试前他一晚上都在做代数题。
senses.why: In everyday school talk the subject name also names the exercise, because the practice is the subject for the student.
senses.whyCN: 在日常校园说法里，学科名也指练习题，因为对学生而言，做题就是这门学科。

intro.en: Algebra carries an Arabic name for restoring broken pieces, a name that describes the method itself.
intro.cn: algebra 带着一个阿拉伯语名称，意为「修复破碎的部分」，这个名称描述的正是方法本身。

items.en: Arabic al-jabr meant the restoring or reunion of broken parts, a term used for setting broken bones.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语 al-jabr 意为修复或重聚破碎的部分，也曾用于接骨。

items.en: The root jabr supplied the idea of forcing something back into place, which became the operation of moving terms across an equation.
items.cn: 词根 jabr 提供「把某物强行归位」的观念，后来成为等式两边移项运算的名称。

items.en: Medieval Latin borrowed the term as algebra, the name of the calculation method in Arabic mathematics.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语借入作 algebra，指阿拉伯数学中这套计算方法的名称。

items.en: Old French passed the word to English, where it named the new art of calculation with unknowns.
items.cn: 古法语把这个词传给英语，用来命名用未知数计算的新技艺。

items.en: English algebra is recorded in the sixteenth century, first as the name of the method rather than the school subject.
items.cn: 英语 algebra 在十六世纪有记录，最初指方法名称，而不是学校科目。

items.en: Modern mathematics widened the word to cover many symbolic systems, from linear to abstract algebra.
items.cn: 现代数学扩大了这个词，使之涵盖从线性代数到抽象代数的众多符号体系。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the algebra family; the near-meaning group gathers neighbouring branches of mathematics.
note.cn: 形近组收 algebra 词族；近义组收相邻的数学分支。

entries.definition: Relating to algebra or to symbolic calculation.
entries.definitionCN: 指与代数或符号计算有关的。

entries.definition: By means of algebra rather than by a graph.
entries.definitionCN: 指用代数方法而不是用图象来解。

entries.definition: A person who works on algebra.
The basic mathematics of numbers and ordinary operations.
entries.definitionCN: 指关于数与普通运算的基础数学。

entries.definition: The mathematics of shape, size and position.
entries.definitionCN: 指关于形状、大小与位置的数学。

entries.definition: The mathematics of continuous change, built on algebra.
entries.definitionCN: 指研究连续变化的数学，建立在代数之上。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the Arabic meaning of reuniting pieces to the visible work of solving.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把阿拉伯语「重聚碎片」的含义，系到看得见的解题动作上。

normal.en: Algebra literally means reuniting broken parts, which is what moving terms does.
normal.cn: algebra 字面意思是把破碎部分重新拼合，这正是移项在做的事。

normal.en: Letters stand in for numbers, so an equation is a sentence with blank spaces.
normal.cn: 字母代替数字，所以一个等式就是一句留有空格的句子。

normal.en: Linear algebra is the algebra of lines and vectors.
normal.cn: linear algebra 是线和向量的代数。

normal.en: Boolean algebra borrows the method for true and false instead of numbers.
normal.cn: 布尔代数把同一方法借去处理真与假，而不是数字。

normal.en: An algebra problem is a broken bone of numbers, waiting to be set back into place.
normal.cn: 一道代数题就是数字的断骨，等着被接回原位。

abstract.en: Picture a broken plate on a table, with the pieces numbered and scattered.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上有一只碎盘子，碎片编号后散落着。

abstract.en: Each equation is a rule for which pieces may be moved next to which.
abstract.cn: 每个等式都是一条规则，说明哪块碎片可以挪到哪块旁边。

abstract.en: When the pieces fit again, the value of the unknown appears in the last joint.
abstract.cn: 碎片重新合上时，未知数的值就显现在最后一道接缝里。

examples.en: Algebra taught her to solve for an unknown step by step.
examples.cn: 代数教会她一步步解出未知数。

examples.en: The engineer used linear algebra to model the bridge.
examples.cn: 工程师用线性代数给这座桥建模。

examples.en: He found the algebra test harder than geometry.
examples.cn: 他觉得代数测验比几何难。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「二姐不惹」——二姐不惹代数题，一见字母就头疼

root: 源自阿拉伯语 al-jabr「修复、重聚破碎部分」（原也指接骨），经中世纪拉丁语 algebra 与古法语 algebre 进入英语；指用符号把问题的碎片重新拼合的数学方法。

sensesIntro.en: The three senses move from the mathematical branch, to a particular symbolic system, to the school exercise that teaches it.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项从数学分支，走到特定的符号体系，再到教授这门学问的学校练习。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: broken pieces lie on a table, and a rule tells you how to join them until the missing piece appears.
core.cn: 核心意象：破碎的片块散在桌上，一条规则告诉你怎么把它们接起来，直到缺失的一块现身。

branches.en: THE BONES: the Arabic name came from setting broken bones, and the subject still sets pieces back in place.
branches.cn: 接骨线：这个阿拉伯语名称来自接骨，而这门学科仍把碎片接回原位。

branches.en: THE LETTER: a symbol takes the place of a number we do not know yet.
branches.cn: 字母线：一个符号代替我们还不知道的数。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: each set of symbols and operations becomes an algebra of its own.
branches.cn: 体系线：每一套符号与运算都成为它自己的一种代数。

branches.en: THE CLASSROOM: the name slides from the subject to the exercises done at a desk.
branches.cn: 课堂线：名称从学科滑到课桌上做的练习题。

branches.en: THE RULE: what all algebras share is a rule for moving symbols without changing the balance.
branches.cn: 规则线：所有代数共享的是同一类规则，在不破坏平衡的前提下移动符号。

intro.en: Algebra is an Arabic loanword with a productive English suffix family; the compounds name branches of the subject.
intro.cn: algebra 是阿拉伯语借词，英语给它长出了能产的后缀词族；复合词则命名各分支。

latinIntro.en: The word reached English through medieval Latin, but its base is Arabic, so Latin family entries are limited.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词经中世纪拉丁语进入英语，但词基来自阿拉伯语，因此拉丁同族条目有限。

items.meaningCN: 用符号表示未知数的数学
items.example: Algebra is taught in middle school.
The Arabic term also meant bone setting.
items.exampleCN: 这个阿拉伯语词也曾指接骨。

items.example: It forms algebraical, an older variant.
items.exampleCN: 它构成较早的变体 algebraical。

items.example: Linear algebra is used in computer graphics.
items.exampleCN: 线性代数用于计算机图形学。

items.meaning: algebra of true and false values
items.exampleCN: 布尔代数是数字电路的基础。

definition_zh: 发抖；震颤；摇晃；担忧
definition_en: to shake slightly and quickly, from cold, fear, or weakness, or to shake as a thing does
core_image: 一双端着碗的手，碗里的水泛起细密的圈
scene: 雪地里，等候的人把手插进袖口，还是止不住地抖。 She was trembling with cold at the bus stop.
sceneCN: 这里 tremble 是「发抖」（第 1 个义项：因寒冷、恐惧或虚弱而轻快地颤）；句意为她在公交站冻得直发抖。袖口里止不住颤的手正是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 现在分词名词化，义为「颤抖」；也可作形容词「发抖的」
同根形容词，义为「颤抖的；胆怯的」
同根名词，义为「轻微震动；颤栗」

senses.title: To shake from cold or fear
senses.definition: to shake quickly and slightly because of cold, fear, or weakness
senses.definitionCN: 因寒冷、恐惧或体弱而轻快地抖动
senses.example: His hands trembled as he opened the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 他拆信时手在发抖。
senses.why: The Latin verb tremere means to shake, and the English word keeps its plainest sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 tremere 意为抖动，英语这个词保留的正是最朴素的那层意思。

senses.title: To shake with strong feeling
senses.definition: to shake because of anger, excitement, or another strong feeling
senses.definitionCN: 因愤怒、激动等强烈情绪而抖
senses.example: She trembled with rage at the words.
senses.exampleCN: 听到那些话她气得发抖。
senses.why: If cold can shake a body, so can feeling, and the verb needs no new shape for it.
senses.whyCN: 寒冷能让身体抖，情绪也能，动词不必换形就能用。

senses.title: To shake, as a thing does
senses.definition: to shake slightly, said of leaves, water, or the ground
senses.definitionCN: 轻微抖动，用于树叶、水面或地面
senses.example: The leaves trembled in the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 树叶在风里轻轻颤动。
senses.why: Latin used tremere of the earth as well as of limbs, so the word still covers things without a will.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语用 tremere 既指四肢也指大地，所以这个词照样管没有意志的东西。

senses.title: To be afraid of what may come
senses.definition: to feel fear or worry about something that may happen
senses.definitionCN: 对可能发生的事感到害怕或不安
senses.example: He trembled at the thought of the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 一想到考试他就心慌。
senses.why: Fear is felt in the body first, so the outward shaking comes to name the inner fear.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧先在身体上显现，于是外在的抖动就被用来指内心的害怕。

senses.title: A shaking of the body or voice
senses.definition: a slight shaking, especially of the body or the voice
senses.definitionCN: 轻度的抖动，尤指身体或嗓音
senses.example: There was a tremble in her voice.
senses.exampleCN: 她的嗓音里有一丝颤抖。
senses.why: The noun is simply the verb turned into a thing, naming the shaking itself.
senses.whyCN: 名词就是把这个动词变成一样东西，给抖动本身起名。

intro.en: The verb comes through French from Latin tremere, to shake, which also gave tremor and tremulous.
intro.cn: 这个动词经法语来自拉丁语 tremere（抖动），tremor 与 tremulous 同出此源。

items.en: Tremere means to shake or quake, and is used of the earth and of limbs alike.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tremere 意为抖动、震动，大地与四肢都用它。

items.en: Tremulus means trembling, and gives English tremulous.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tremulus 意为发抖的，生出英语 tremulous。

items.en: Old French trembler keeps the plain sense of shaking with cold or fear.
items.cn: 古法语 trembler 保留因寒冷或恐惧而抖的朴素义。

items.en: English borrows the verb early and uses it for both bodies and leaves.
items.cn: 英语很早就借入这个动词，既用于人，也用于树叶。

items.en: The noun form appears later, usually of the voice or the hands.
items.cn: 名词形式出现较晚，多指嗓音或手。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the trem- root of shaking, while the near-meaning group gathers other verbs of unsteady motion.
note.cn: 形近组共用表示抖动的 trem- 词根，近义组汇集其他表示不稳震动的动词。

entries.definition: a slight shaking movement
shaking slightly, or timid
the act of shaking
to step heavily on something
to shake from cold or fear
to shake violently, of the earth
to move quickly to and fro
to shake from horror or cold

normalIntro.en: The trem- stem turns up in tremor and tremulous, so learn it once.
normalIntro.cn: trem- 词干也出现在 tremor 与 tremulous 里，记一次就够。

normal.en: Tremere is to shake, and tremble is the plain English verb from it.
normal.cn: tremere 是抖动，tremble 就是它变来的朴素英语动词。

normal.en: Tremor is the noun for a shaking, often of the ground.
normal.cn: tremor 是抖动的名词，多指地面。

normal.en: The past tense is trembled, with -ed after the l.
normal.cn: 过去式是 trembled，l 后加 -ed。

normal.en: A tremulous voice is one that is shaking.
normal.cn: tremulous voice 就是发抖的嗓音。

normal.en: Shiver is colder, shudder is more about horror, tremble sits between.
normal.cn: shiver 更偏冷，shudder 更偏恶心，tremble 居中。

abstract.en: Picture a cup of water held by two hands that will not keep still.
abstract.cn: 想象一双手端着一杯水，怎么也拿不稳。

abstract.en: Watch the circles spread from the rim inward.
abstract.cn: 看着水纹从杯壁往里散。

abstract.en: Then let a leaf do the same thing on a bare branch.
abstract.cn: 再让一片叶子在光枝上做同样的动作。

examples.en: Her voice trembled as she read the letter aloud.
examples.cn: 她大声读信时声音在发颤。

examples.en: The old bridge trembled under the weight of the lorry.
examples.cn: 老桥在卡车的重量下颤动。

examples.en: He trembled at the thought of speaking in public.
examples.cn: 一想到公开发言他就心慌。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「吞不乐」——冻得吞下不开心，浑身抖个不停。

root: 拉丁语 tremere（抖动），经古法语 trembler 进入英语；同族有 tremor、tremulous

sensesIntro.en: One small, fast shaking, whether it runs through a body, a leaf, or the ground.
sensesIntro.cn: 就是一种又小又快的抖动，无论在身体里、叶子上还是地面上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands holding a cup that will not stay still.
core.cn: 核心意象：一双手端着怎么也端不稳的杯子。

branches.en: The body senses, first from cold and fear, then from anger and joy.
branches.cn: 身体义：先因寒冷与恐惧，再因愤怒与激动。

branches.en: The object sense, where leaves and bridges shake too.
branches.cn: 物体义：叶子与桥也会抖。

branches.en: The inner sense, where only the feeling shakes.
branches.cn: 内心义：抖的只是那份心情。

branches.en: The noun sense, a name for the shaking itself.
branches.cn: 名词义：给这种抖动本身起名。

branches.en: The default image: cold hands at a bus stop.
branches.cn: 默认画面：车站上冻僵的手。

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb of shaking with a frequentative air, worn down by French.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「抖动」动词，带反复意味，经法语磨圆了形状。

latinIntro.en: Trem- stays visible in tremor and tremulous, both closer to the Latin.
latinIntro.cn: trem- 在 tremor 与 tremulous 里仍然看得见，两者都更接近拉丁原形。

items.example: The stem gives tremor and tremulous.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干生出 tremor 与 tremulous。

items.meaningCN: 经法语来自拉丁 -ulare 的动词词尾

items.exampleCN: 一阵震动震得窗户直响。

items.example: The dog trembled in the rain.
The bridge trembled for a moment.

items.meaningCN: 构成现在分词与动名词

definition_zh: 乘；使成倍增加；增多；繁殖；增殖
definition_en: to perform multiplication, or to increase greatly in number
core_image: 两堆积木一层层往上叠，层数越高，块数翻得越快
scene: 两个孩子把积木一层层往上叠，越叠越高。 If you multiply the side length by three, the area grows ninefold.
sceneCN: 这里 multiply 指「做乘法，把某个量乘上另一个量」（第 1 个义项：乘）；句意为把边长乘以三，面积就增大到九倍。图中可辨识物件：积木、两层堆叠、孩子的手、量尺；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: To perform multiplication
senses.definition: to find the product of two or more numbers
senses.definitionCN: 求两个或更多数的乘积
senses.example: If you multiply the side length by three, the area grows ninefold.
senses.exampleCN: 把边长乘以三，面积就增大到九倍。
senses.why: multiply is the verb of folding equal copies together, and arithmetic uses it for the operation that counts those copies.
senses.whyCN: multiply 是把相同副本叠合起来的动词，算术用它来指清点这些副本的运算。

senses.title: To increase greatly
senses.definition: to make something much larger in number or amount
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物的数量或数额大大增加
senses.example: The new road multiplied the number of visitors ten times over.
senses.exampleCN: 新修的公路让访客数量增加了十倍。
senses.why: outside arithmetic the verb keeps the picture of many copies appearing: one cause produces a crowd of results.
senses.whyCN: 在算术之外，这个动词保留「许多副本出现」的画面：一个原因产生一大群结果。

senses.title: To grow in number
senses.definition: to become more numerous without an outside agent
senses.definitionCN: 在没有外来施动者的情况下变得更多
senses.example: Problems multiplied while the team was away.
senses.exampleCN: 团队不在的时候，问题越来越多。
senses.why: the intransitive use shifts the focus from someone making more to things simply becoming many.
senses.whyCN: 不及物用法把焦点从「有人使变多」转到「事物自己变多」。

senses.title: To breed
senses.definition: to produce offspring and so increase a population
senses.definitionCN: 产生后代，从而使种群数量增加
senses.example: The rabbits multiplied faster than the gardeners could catch them.
senses.exampleCN: 兔子繁殖得比园丁抓得还快。
senses.why: breeding is increase by copies of living things, so the old verb for increase became the verb for breeding.
senses.whyCN: 繁育就是活物靠副本增多，于是那个表示「增多」的老动词成了繁育的动词。

senses.title: For cells to divide and increase
senses.definition: to increase in number by cell division
senses.definitionCN: 通过细胞分裂而数量增多
senses.example: The cells multiply until the wound is covered.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞不断增殖，直到伤口被覆盖。
senses.why: cell division repeats copies at a microscopic scale, and the arithmetic verb describes that repetition exactly.
senses.whyCN: 细胞分裂在微观尺度上重复副本，算术里的这个动词正描述这种重复。

senses.title: To multiply out
senses.definition: to expand a product of bracketed expressions by multiplying every term
senses.definitionCN: 把括号表达式的乘积逐项相乘展开
senses.example: Multiply out the brackets before collecting like terms.
senses.exampleCN: 先把括号乘开，再合并同类项。
senses.why: the particle 'out' marks the unfolding of a folded product, the reverse of the folding image inside the word.
senses.whyCN: 「乘开」里的「开」正标出把折起的乘积展开，与词内「折叠」的形象相反。

senses.title: To multiply by a number
senses.definition: to apply a particular factor to a quantity
senses.definitionCN: 对某个量施加一个特定的倍数
senses.example: Multiply the reading by ten to get the true value.
senses.exampleCN: 把读数乘以十，就得到真实值。
senses.why: this is the everyday phrasing of the operation, with the factor named after the preposition by.
senses.whyCN: 这是这项运算的日常说法，倍数在介词之后点出来。

senses.title: To multiply one's chances
senses.definition: to make an opportunity or risk much more likely
senses.definitionCN: 使某个机会或风险的可能性大大增加
senses.example: Two applications multiplied her chances of being accepted.
senses.exampleCN: 投出两份申请，让她被录取的机会成倍增加。
senses.why: chances behave like countable copies, so making more of them feels like multiplication rather than simple addition.
senses.whyCN: 机会像可数的副本，把机会变多感觉像相乘而不是简单相加。

intro.en: Multiply comes from Latin multiplicare 'to make many-fold', from multiplex, built on multus 'many' and plicare 'to fold'. English took the verb through Old French multiplier.
intro.cn: multiply 来自拉丁 multiplicare「使成多重」，出自 multiplex，由 multus「多」与 plicare「折叠」构成。英语经古法语 multiplier 引入这个动词。

items.en: Multus meant 'many'. It also lies behind multiple, multitude and the first half of multiply.
items.cn: multus 意为「多」。它也是 multiple、multitude 以及 multiply 前半部分的来源。

items.en: Plicare meant 'to fold'; the same verb gives explicit 'unfolded', complicate 'folded together' and duplicate 'folded twice'.
items.cn: plicare 意为「折叠」；同一个动词给出 explicit「展开的」、complicate「折在一起」与 duplicate「折两次」。

items.en: Multus plus -plex made multiplex 'many-fold'; the adjective pictures layers folded onto one another.
items.cn: multus 加 -plex 构成 multiplex「多重的」；这个形容词描画一层层叠在一起。

items.en: The verb multiplicare meant 'to make many-fold, increase', and arithmetic narrowed it to repeated addition.
items.cn: 动词 multiplicare 意为「使成多重、使增多」，算术把它收窄为重复相加。

items.en: Old French multiplier carried the verb into English in the thirteenth century, first as 'increase' and then as the arithmetic operation.
items.cn: 古法语 multiplier 在十三世纪把这个动词带入英语，先表示「增多」，后表示算术运算。

items.en: The first English date for the arithmetic sense is approximate; the Latin verb and its parts are securely attested.
items.cn: 算术义在英语中的最早年代为约数；这个拉丁动词及其构件则有可靠记录。

note.en: The first group shares the folding root and is easily confused; the second group names other kinds of growth.
note.cn: 第一组共享那个表示「折叠」的词根，容易混淆；第二组是其他增长方式。

entries.definition: A number divisible by another, or an adjective meaning many; it names a result, not the act of multiplying.
entries.definitionCN: 指能被另一个数整除的数，或形容词「多个的」；命名的是结果，不是相乘的动作。

entries.definition: The noun of the operation; it names the act or the process that multiply performs.
entries.definitionCN: 这项运算的名词；命名 multiply 所执行的动作或过程。

entries.definition: The quality of being many; it counts kinds or instances rather than performing a product.
entries.definitionCN: 指「多」的性质；数的是种类或实例，不做乘积。

entries.definition: Many-fold or having many parts; it keeps the old adjective without becoming a verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指多重的或有许多部分的；保留老形容词，并未变成动词。

entries.definition: From explicare 'to unfold'; it shares plicare and means fully stated, with no arithmetic sense.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 explicare「展开」；共享 plicare，意为明确说出的，没有算术义。

entries.definition: To become larger or more; it lacks the sense of equal copies folded together.
entries.definitionCN: 指变大或变多；不含相同副本叠合的意思。

entries.definition: To increase quickly by producing new parts; it stresses spreading, not the arithmetic rule.
entries.definitionCN: 指通过产生新部分而迅速增多；强调扩散，而非算术规则。

entries.definition: To produce offspring; multiplying can describe the resulting rise in numbers.
entries.definitionCN: 指产生后代；multiplying 可以描述由此带来的数量上升。

entries.definition: To grow in size or scope; it does not imply counting equal groups.
entries.definitionCN: 指规模或范围扩大；不含清点相同组的意思。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin pieces, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁构件、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: multus 'many' plus plicare 'fold': to fold many copies into one product.
normal.cn: multus「多」加 plicare「折」：把许多副本折成一个乘积。

normal.en: The family runs multiply, multiplication, multiple, multiplicity and multiplier.
normal.cn: 同族词有 multiply、multiplication、multiple、multiplicity 与 multiplier。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: multiply by, multiply out, multiply in number.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：乘以、乘开、数量增多。

normal.en: Multiply out is the reverse of the folding inside the word: layers come apart into terms.
normal.cn: multiply out 与词内的「折」相反：层叠散开成为一项一项。

normal.en: Rabbits are the classic example of the breeding sense: they multiply faster than anyone can count.
normal.cn: 兔子是繁殖义的经典例子：它们增多得比谁数得都快。

abstract.en: Picture one brick that becomes two, then four, then eight, in the same minute.
abstract.cn: 想象一块砖在同一分钟里变成两块、四块、八块。

abstract.en: Picture a rumour spreading from one table to every table in the hall.
abstract.cn: 想象一个传闻从一桌传到大厅里的每一桌。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of brackets opening outward like a pair of hands.
abstract.cn: 想象一对括号像两只手一样向外张开。

examples.en: Multiply the length by the width to get the area.
examples.cn: 把长乘以宽就得到面积。

examples.en: Bacteria multiply rapidly in warm, moist conditions.
examples.cn: 细菌在温暖潮湿的条件下迅速繁殖。

examples.en: Multiply out the brackets and then simplify the result.
examples.cn: 把括号乘开，然后化简结果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「满多倍」——一层层叠成多倍 → 乘、成倍增多

root: 拉丁 multus「多」+ plicare「折叠」→ multiplex「多重的」→ multiplicare「使增多」→ 古法语 multiplier → 英语 multiply。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one verb of folding copies: making a product, making much more, becoming many, breeding, cells dividing, opening brackets, applying a factor and swelling one's chances.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一个「把副本叠起来」的动词：求乘积、使多得多、自身变多、繁殖、细胞分裂、打开括号、施加倍数，以及把机会撑大。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two stacks of blocks folded upward, the count rising faster than the height.
core.cn: 核心意象：两堆积木层层往上叠，块数比高度涨得更快。

branches.en: THE OPERATION: finding a product, and applying a named factor to a quantity.
branches.cn: 运算：求乘积，以及对某个量施加点名的倍数。

branches.en: MAKING MORE: swelling a number greatly, and swelling someone's chances.
branches.cn: 使更多：让数量大大增加，也让机会大大增加。

branches.en: BECOMING MANY: problems and troubles simply grow in number.
branches.cn: 自己变多：问题与麻烦就这样越来越多。

branches.en: LIFE COPIES ITSELF: rabbits breeding and cells dividing are the same arithmetic in flesh.
branches.cn: 生命复制自身：兔子繁殖与细胞分裂，是同一套算术长在血肉里。

branches.en: OPEN THE BRACKETS: multiply out unfolds the product term by term.
branches.cn: 打开括号：乘开把乘积一项一项地展开。

intro.en: Multiply is a Latin verb of folding many together; its pieces and endings build a large English family.
intro.cn: multiply 是一个拉丁动词，意为把许多层折在一起；其构件与词尾构成一个很大的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin multus and plicare give multiple, multiplex, multiplicity, explicit, complicate and duplicate; the verb ending -are became English -ify through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 multus 与 plicare 衍生 multiple、multiplex、multiplicity、explicit、complicate 与 duplicate；动词词尾 -are 经法语变成英语的 -ify。

items.example: The adjective stays in English as multiplex.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词以 multiplex 的形式留在英语里。

items.example: The Latin verb is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词是直接来源。

items.meaning: to make a product; to increase
a number that contains another exactly
items.example: Six is a multiple of two.
The multiplicity of voices filled the room.

items.meaning: the number or factor that multiplies
items.exampleCN: 这个乘数把每个分数都抬高了。

items.meaningCN: 表示「使成为」的动词后缀
items.example: It also appears in simplify and amplify.
items.exampleCN: 它也出现在 simplify 与 amplify 里。

definition_zh: 证明……正当；为……辩护；使合理化；调整使排满（排版）
definition_en: to show that something is right or reasonable, or to give a good reason for it
core_image: 有人举起一张纸，一条一条向对面的人解释为什么这样做没错
scene: 会议室里被质问的一方把证据摊开，逐条说明当初的决定为什么合理。 Nothing can justify that much expense on one dinner.
sceneCN: 这里 justify 是「证明……正当」（第 1 个义项：给出理由说明某事合理），句意为没有任何理由能为一顿晚饭花那么多钱开脱。画面里的物件：会议室、证据文件、对面的听众。

pos.zh: 动词：证明正当；为……辩解；使合理；（排版）使两端对齐

derivatives.zh: 由 justify 加 -cation 构成，义为「辩护；正当理由」
由 justify 加 -ed 构成，义为「有正当理由的」
由 justify 加 -able 构成，义为「可辩解的」
加前缀 un- 构成，义为「无正当理由的」

senses.title: To show that something is right
senses.definition: to give reasons that show an action or claim is right or reasonable
senses.definitionCN: 给出理由以证明某行为或主张合理
senses.example: How do you justify spending so much on a phone?
senses.exampleCN: 你凭什么为花这么多钱买手机找理由？
senses.why: The word sets a thing on the scale of right and asks whether it balances.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把一件事放上「正当」的秤，问它是否配平。

senses.title: To defend against criticism
senses.definition: to answer criticism by defending a choice or statement
senses.definitionCN: 通过辩护某个选择或说法来回应批评
senses.example: The manager justified his decision to the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 经理向全队为自己的决定作了辩解。
senses.why: Justifying is talking back to an accusation with reasons.
senses.whyCN: 辩解就是用理由回应一项指责。

senses.title: To be a good reason for
senses.definition: to be the reason that makes something acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 本身构成使某事可接受的理由
senses.example: The delay was justified by the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 这次延误因暴风雨而有其理由。
senses.why: Here the subject is the reason itself, not the speaker.
senses.whyCN: 这里作主语的是理由本身，而不是说话的人。

senses.title: To set text flush at the margins
senses.definition: in printing, to space text so that both edges line up
senses.definitionCN: 排版中调整字距，使左右两边都对齐
senses.example: The columns are justified so the page looks tidy.
senses.exampleCN: 各栏都两端对齐，页面显得整齐。
senses.why: Typesetting sets lines to exact margins, the same exactness the word always carried.
senses.whyCN: 排版把行对齐到精确的边界，正是这个词一直带有的「精确」。

senses.title: To prove oneself right by result
senses.definition: to be shown right by later events
senses.definitionCN: 指后来的事实说明当初是对的
senses.example: The final score justified the coach's choice.
senses.exampleCN: 最终比分证明了教练的选择。
senses.why: Later facts can do the weighing that argument could not.
senses.whyCN: 后来发生的事实能做论证做不到的那次称量。

senses.title: To declare someone righteous
senses.definition: in theology, to declare a person righteous before God
senses.definitionCN: 神学中指宣告某人在神面前为义
senses.example: The doctrine says faith alone justifies the believer.
senses.exampleCN: 该教义说唯凭信使信徒称义。
senses.why: The theological sense is a declaration of rightness rather than a proof.
senses.whyCN: 神学义是一种宣告其为义，而不是去证明。

intro.en: Justify is Latin justus, right, plus facere, to make: to make right or to show as right.
intro.cn: justify 是拉丁语 justus「正当的」加 facere「做」：使之正当，或显示其为正当。

items.en: justificare meant to make just or to do justice, from justus and facere.
items.cn: justificare 意为使之公正或伸张正义，由 justus 与 facere 组成。

items.en: The -fic- element is a form of facere, to make or do.
items.cn: -fic- 部分是 facere「做」的形式，广见于 -ify 动词。

items.en: English borrowed justify in the fourteenth century for legal defence.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 justify，最初用于法律辩护。

items.en: The theological sense of being declared righteous developed in the Reformation.
items.cn: 「称义」的神学义在宗教改革时期发展起来。

items.en: The printing sense arrived with mechanical typesetting.
items.cn: 排版义随机械排字而来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -ify pattern and the justice root; the near-meaning group holds verbs of defending and explaining.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -ify 构词与 justice 词根；近义组收辩护与解释类动词。

entries.definition: Fairness or the court system.
entries.definitionCN: 同源名词，义为「正义；司法」。

entries.definition: One who gives a defence.
entries.definitionCN: 由 justify 加 -er 构成，指辩解者。

entries.definition: A reason given in defence.
entries.definitionCN: 派生名词，义为「正当理由」。

entries.definition: To protect or argue for something attacked.
entries.definitionCN: 指抵御或为受攻者辩护。

entries.definition: To make something clear.
entries.definitionCN: 指把事情说清楚，不必涉及对错。

entries.definition: To try to lessen the blame for something.

normalIntro.en: These hooks run from justus plus facere to justified text on a page.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从 justus 加 facere 走到页面上两端对齐的文字。

normal.en: Justify is just plus -ify, which comes from facere, to make.
normal.cn: justify 是 just 加 -ify，后者来自 facere「做」。

normal.en: The -ify ending also appears in testify and simplify.
normal.cn: -ify 词尾也见于 testify 与 simplify。

normal.en: Justify doing something is the common pattern.
normal.cn: justify doing something 是常见搭配。

normal.en: The noun is justification, not justifation.
normal.cn: 名词是 justification，不是 justifation。

normal.en: Justified text lines up on both sides.
normal.cn: justified text 指左右两边都对齐的文字。

abstract.en: To justify is to hand the scale a weight that balances.
abstract.cn: 辩护就是往秤另一头放上配得上的砝码。

abstract.en: A reason that fits exactly is justice at the level of argument.
abstract.cn: 恰好配平的理由，就是论证层面的正义。

abstract.en: Some things cannot be weighed at all.
abstract.cn: 有些事根本没法上秤。

examples.en: Nothing can justify hiding the report.
examples.cn: 没有任何理由能为隐瞒报告开脱。

examples.en: She was justified in refusing the offer.
examples.cn: 她拒绝这个提议是有道理的。

examples.en: Justify the whole paragraph to make it look clean.
examples.cn: 把整段两端对齐，看起来更整齐。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「just 我 fi」—— 站得正，才敢说「我没错」

root: 拉丁语 justus「正当的」+ facere「做」→ justificare「使之正当」→ 英语 justify；名词 justification。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses: showing something right, defending it, being the reason for it, aligning text, being proved right, and being declared righteous.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项：证明合理、为决定辩护、构成理由、文字两端对齐、以结果证明，以及宗教上的「称义」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: reasons laid on a scale until it balances.
core.cn: 核心意象：把理由放到秤上，直到配平。

branches.en: THE SCALE: reasons heavy enough to hold the act up.
branches.cn: 秤这条线：理由够重，撑得住那个行为。

branches.en: THE MEETING: a decision explained to those who question it.
branches.cn: 会议这条线：向质疑者解释决定。

branches.en: THE PAGE: every line lands on both margins.
branches.cn: 页面这条线：每一行都落在两边边界上。

branches.en: THE SCOREBOARD: the result that settles the argument.
branches.cn: 记分牌这条线：结果把争论定下。

branches.en: THE PULPIT: the doctrine of being made righteous.
branches.cn: 讲坛这条线：称义的教义。

intro.en: Justify is just plus the Latin verb ending -ify, from facere.
intro.cn: justify 是 just 加拉丁动词词尾 -ify，源自 facere。

latinIntro.en: The Latin relatives come from jus through justus and from facere.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词来自 jus（经 justus）与 facere。

definition_zh: 合理地；相当地；以公道价格
definition_en: in a fair and sensible way; to a moderate degree; at a fair price
core_image: 天平两端轻轻持平，价钱与品质对得上
scene: 旧书店的柜台前，顾客翻看价签，觉得价钱与书况相称。 The shop sells reasonably priced second-hand books.
sceneCN: 这里 reasonably 修饰 priced，是「以公道价格」（第 3 个义项：价钱合理）；句意为这家店卖的二手书价格公道。画面里可留意：持平的天平、与书况相称的价签。

pos.zh: 合理地；相当地；以公道价格

senses.title: In a fair and sensible way
senses.definition: in a way that is fair, sensible, and based on good judgment
senses.definitionCN: 以公平、明智且基于良好判断的方式
senses.example: She reasonably refused the unfair offer.
senses.exampleCN: 她合理地拒绝了那个不公平的提议。
senses.why: Reason is the base, and the suffix -able marks what fits reason, so the adverb describes acting in line with reason.
senses.whyCN: reason 是词根，后缀 -able 表示「合乎理性的」，因此这个副词描述按理性行事。

senses.title: To a moderate degree
senses.definition: to a fair but not extreme degree, more than a little
senses.definitionCN: 达到公道而不极端的程度，多于一点
senses.example: The exam was reasonably difficult.
senses.exampleCN: 这次考试相当难。
senses.why: Fairness of judgment weakened into fairness of degree, so the word came to mean fairly or quite.
senses.whyCN: 判断上的「公道」弱化为程度上的「适中」，于是这个词有了「相当」的意思。

senses.title: At a fair price
senses.definition: at a price that is fair for what is offered
senses.definitionCN: 以对所提供之物而言公道的价格
senses.example: The flat is reasonably priced for the area.
senses.exampleCN: 就这个地段而言，这套公寓价格公道。
senses.why: A price judged fair by reason is a price that reason approves, so the adverb commonly attaches to the word priced.
senses.whyCN: 经理性判定为公道的价格，就是理性认可的价格，因此这个副词常与 priced 连用。

intro.en: Reasonably grows from the Latin root for reckoning, passing through French into English and taking two suffixes, one for fitness and one for manner.
intro.cn: reasonably 从拉丁语「计算」的词根出发，经法语进入英语，并加上两个后缀：一个表「合乎」，一个表方式。

items.en: Ratio meant reckoning or account, the root of reason and of every fair judgment.
items.cn: ratio 意为计算或账目，是 reason 与一切公道判断的词根。

items.en: Old French raison carried the Latin root into English as reason, the power to judge.
items.cn: 古法语 raison 把拉丁词根带入英语，成为 reason，即判断的能力。

items.en: The suffix -able, from Latin -abilis, means capable of or fit for, giving reasonable.
items.cn: 后缀 -able 源自拉丁 -abilis，意为「能够……的、合乎……的」，由此构成 reasonable。

items.en: The native suffix -ly turns the adjective into an adverb of manner and degree.
items.cn: 本族后缀 -ly 把形容词变为表方式与程度的副词。

items.en: Modern English uses reasonably for fair judgment, for a moderate degree, and for a fair price.
items.cn: 现代英语用 reasonably 表公道判断、表适中程度，也表公道的价格。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the adjective base and two related forms; the near-meaning group gathers degree words and words of fairness.
note.cn: 形近组收形容词原形与两个同族词；近义组收程度词与表公道的词。

entries.definition: Sensible and fair, the adjective base.
entries.definitionCN: 明智而公道的，形容词原形。

entries.definition: Based on careful thought.
The power to think and judge.
To a moderate degree.
Within reasonable limits.
In a practical and wise way.
With good reason.

normalIntro.en: The word is reason plus able plus ly: a judgment that fits reason, delivered in a fair manner.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 reason 加 able 再加 ly：合乎理性的判断，以公道的方式做出。

normal.en: Reason is the root; reasonable adds -able; reasonably adds -ly.
normal.cn: 词根是 reason，加 able 成 reasonable，再加 ly 成 reasonably。

normal.en: A reasonably priced item is priced in a way reason approves.
normal.cn: reasonably priced 指价格经得起理性衡量。

normal.en: Reasonably well means fairly well, not very well.
normal.cn: reasonably well 指相当好，而不是非常好。

normal.en: The -ly ending tells you the word describes how something is done.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ly 提醒你这个词描述做事的方式。

normal.en: Split it as reason + able + ly to keep the spelling right.
normal.cn: 把它拆成 reason 加 able 加 ly，拼写就不容易错。

abstract.en: Reasonableness is a scale: fair first, then moderate, never extreme.
abstract.cn: 合理性是一把尺：先讲公道，再讲适中，从不走极端。

abstract.en: To act reasonably is to leave room for the other side.
abstract.cn: 行事合理，就是给对方留出余地。

abstract.en: A fair price is reason made visible in numbers.
abstract.cn: 公道的价格，是理性在数字上的显形。

examples.en: She reasonably refused the unfair offer.
examples.cn: 她合理地拒绝了那个不公平的提议。

examples.en: The exam was reasonably difficult.
examples.cn: 这次考试相当难。

examples.en: The flat is reasonably priced for the area.
examples.cn: 就这个地段而言，这套公寓价格公道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 reason（理性）加 able（能）加 ly（地）：能按理性来，就是合理地；程度适中，就是相当地。

root: 拉丁 ratio（计算、账目）→ 古法语 raison → 英语 reason（理性）→ reasonable（合理的）→ reasonably（合理地）；同族有 reasoning、reasonableness。

sensesIntro.en: The core is judgment by reason; the senses move from a fair manner to a moderate degree to a fair price.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「按理性判断」；义项从公道行事，到适中程度，再到公道价格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance whose two pans rest level, price matching quality.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平两端持平，价钱与品质相称。

branches.en: a judgment weighed on a balance
branches.cn: 在天平上称过的判断

branches.en: a needle resting mid-scale
branches.cn: 指针停在刻度中段

branches.en: a price tag that matches the goods
branches.cn: 与货物相称的价签

branches.en: fair in manner and moderate in degree
branches.cn: 方式公道，程度适中

branches.en: a moderate amount and a fair price
branches.cn: 适中的量与公道的价

intro.en: The word grows from the Latin root for reckoning through two English suffixes, one for fitness and one for manner.
intro.cn: 这个词从拉丁语「计算」的词根出发，经过两个英语后缀：一个表「合乎」，一个表方式。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin ratio, and the suffix -able goes back to Latin -abilis.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是拉丁 ratio，后缀 -able 可追溯到拉丁 -abilis。

definition_zh: 射击；子弹；照片；投篮
definition_en: the firing of a gun, a small projectile, a photograph, or an attempt to score
core_image: 枪口一闪，子弹飞出，远处靶心留下一个洞
scene: 远处传来一声枪响。 A shot rang out in the distance.
sceneCN: 这里 shot 是「射击」（第 1 个义项）；句意：远处传来一声枪响。

senses.title: A firing
senses.definition: the act of firing a gun or other weapon
senses.definitionCN: 开枪或用其他武器发射的动作
senses.example: A shot rang out in the distance.
senses.exampleCN: 远处传来一声枪响。
senses.why: This is the earliest and most physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最早也最具体的义项。

senses.title: A projectile
senses.definition: a small metal ball or pellet fired from a gun
senses.definitionCN: 从枪中射出的小金属球或弹丸
senses.example: The box held a dozen lead shots.
senses.exampleCN: 盒子里装着十几颗铅弹。
senses.why: The thing fired is named after the act.
senses.whyCN: 被射出的东西沿用了这一动作的名称。

senses.title: A photograph
senses.definition: a photograph, especially one taken quickly
senses.definitionCN: 照片，尤指快速拍下的一张
senses.example: She took a shot of the sunset.
senses.exampleCN: 她拍了一张日落照片。
senses.why: A camera fires a picture as a gun fires a bullet.
senses.whyCN: 相机拍下照片，就像枪射出子弹。

senses.title: A scoring attempt
senses.definition: an attempt to score in a sport
senses.definitionCN: 体育比赛中一次得分尝试
senses.example: His last shot missed the basket.
senses.exampleCN: 他最后一投没有命中篮筐。
senses.why: The sport sense extends the idea of one quick attempt.
senses.whyCN: 体育义项延伸了「一次快速尝试」的概念。

intro.en: Shot is an old Germanic word for something thrown or fired.
intro.cn: shot 是日耳曼语中表示被投出或射出之物的古老词。

items.en: Sceot meant a projectile or missile.
items.cn: sceot 意为投射物或飞弹。

items.en: The verb sceotan meant to shoot.
items.cn: 动词 sceotan 意为射击。

items.en: Shot named an arrow or a stone from a weapon.
items.cn: shot 指箭或武器射出的石块。

definition_zh: 比较；对比；比喻；可比之处

senses.title: Not even: one left over after pairing
senses.titleCN: 奇数：两两配对后多出一个
senses.definition: of a number: having one left over when divided by two
senses.definitionCN: 指数目：被二除后余一
senses.example: Three is an odd number, so one chair is always empty.
senses.exampleCN: 三是奇数，所以总会空出一把椅子。
senses.why: Old Norse oddi meant 'a third or additional number', the unit beyond an even count. The oldest English sense is exactly this arithmetic one.
senses.whyCN: 古诺斯语 oddi 意为“第三个数、额外的数”，即成双之外多出的那一单位。英语最古老的义项正是这个算术义。

senses.title: Unpaired: the single one of a pair
senses.titleCN: 落单：一对里剩下的那只
senses.definition: of one of a pair: left without its partner and therefore unusable as a set
senses.definitionCN: 指一对中的一只：失去配对的另一只，因此无法成套使用
senses.example: One odd glove lay on the bench for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 一只落单的手套在长椅上放了一周。
senses.why: The 'one over' count becomes a concrete object: if a pair is a set of two, the unit left over is the odd one, and the pair is broken.
senses.whyCN: “多出一个”的计数变成具体物件：一对是成双的集合，剩下的那一单位就是 odd，这一对也就散了。

senses.title: Occasional, not regular: odd jobs and odd moments
senses.titleCN: 零星的：不定时的零工与零碎时间
senses.definition: not forming part of a regular pattern; happening now and then
senses.definitionCN: 不构成规律的一部分；偶尔发生
senses.example: He takes odd jobs in the holidays to pay for books.
senses.exampleCN: 他假期打零工来买书。
senses.why: A job that does not belong to a regular set is the 'extra' unit again: isolated, unpaired, scattered through the week.
senses.whyCN: 不属于固定一套的活计又是那个“多余单位”：孤立、不成对、散落在一周里。

senses.title: Strange, peculiar
senses.definition: unusual or unexpected in a way that makes people uneasy or curious
senses.definitionCN: 不寻常或出乎意料，让人不安或好奇
senses.example: It was odd that the door stood unlocked all night.
senses.exampleCN: 门整夜没锁，这有点古怪。
senses.why: The 'strange' sense is recorded from the 1580s and grows from 'the odd one out': what does not fit the set draws attention and looks wrong.
senses.whyCN: “古怪”义自 16 世纪 80 年代有记录，从“落单的那一个”生长出来：不合群的东西招人注意，也显得不对劲。

senses.title: Slightly more than: forty-odd
senses.definition: used after a number to mean 'and a little more', as in forty-odd people
senses.definitionCN: 用在数字后表示“再多一点”，如 forty-odd people
senses.example: Thirty-odd people signed up for the night walk.
senses.exampleCN: 三十多个人报名参加了夜行。
senses.why: Here the leftover unit is attached to a round number: the count passes the round figure by an odd remainder, so the 'extra' becomes an approximation.
senses.whyCN: 这里多出的单位附在整数后面：数目超出整数一点点零头，于是“多余”变成约数。

senses.title: The odd one out: set apart from the group
senses.titleCN: 格格不入：被排除在群体之外
senses.definition: the person or thing that does not match the rest of a group
senses.definitionCN: 与群体其余成员不相配的人或物
senses.example: She was the odd one out in a family of musicians.
senses.exampleCN: 在一个音乐家家庭里，她是个例外。
senses.why: A set works by pairing; whoever cannot be paired is visibly separate. Being 'the odd one out' is the social version of the broken pair.
senses.whyCN: 一组东西靠配对成立；配不上对的那个就明显独立在外。“落单者”就是破碎配对的社会版本。

senses.title: Odds and ends: leftover scraps
senses.titleCN: 零碎杂物：用剩的边角料
senses.definition: in odds and ends, small useful items left over from larger things
senses.definitionCN: 用于 odds and ends，指大件用剩的小而有用之物
senses.example: The drawer was full of odds and ends: buttons, wire and old stamps.
senses.exampleCN: 抽屉里塞满零碎东西：纽扣、铁丝和旧邮票。
senses.why: The plural odds means unequal remainders; combined with ends, it names the scraps that no longer belong to any complete set.
senses.whyCN: 复数 odds 指不相等的余数；与 ends 连用，就命名了那些不再属于任何完整套组的边角料。

senses.title: Odds: the chances of an outcome
senses.titleCN: 赔率与可能性：成败的差距
senses.definition: in the plural noun odds, the probability of one result rather than another, used in betting and in general prediction
senses.definitionCN: 复数名词 odds 指某一结果相对另一结果的可能性，用于赌博与一般预测
senses.example: The odds are against a rookie winning this tournament.
senses.exampleCN: 新手赢得这次比赛的可能性不大。
senses.why: Odds began as unequal numbers, a ratio that is not even. Betting turned that imbalance into a measure of chance: the odds are the unevenness of outcomes.
senses.whyCN: odds 起初指不相等的数，即不成偶的比例。博彩把这种不平衡变成机会的量度：赔率就是结果之间的不均等。

senses.title: Odd Fellow: a member of a friendly society
senses.titleCN: Odd Fellow：互助会会员（历史用法）
senses.definition: in the name Odd Fellows, a member of a fraternal benefit society that grew from local clubs in the late 18th century and was formally organised in 1813
senses.definitionCN: 在 Odd Fellows 这一名称中，指兄弟互助会的成员；该会由 18 世纪末的地方社团发展而来，1813 年正式组织
senses.example: He joined the Odd Fellows in 1813 and paid a small weekly sum for sickness cover.
senses.exampleCN: 他于 1813 年加入 Odd Fellows，每周缴一小笔钱以备生病。
senses.why: The society's name uses odd in the older sense of 'unusual companions': members were fellows of an odd sort, set apart from ordinary clubs. Odd Fellows is recorded as a local society late in the 18th century.
senses.whyCN: 这个会名用的是 odd 较旧的“奇怪的伙伴”义：成员是些“古怪的同伴”，与普通社团不同。Odd Fellows 作为地方社团记录于 18 世纪晚期。

intro.en: Odd is recorded around 1300 from Old Norse oddi 'a third or additional number'. The Norse word literally meant 'point of land, angle', and the step from 'point' to 'third number' is a development special to that language, so it is best marked as generally accepted.
intro.cn: odd 约于 1300 年从古诺斯语 oddi“第三个数、额外的数”进入英语。这个诺斯语词字面是“尖角、土地的一角”，而从“尖点”到“第三个数”这一步是该语言特有的发展，故宜标为“一般认为”。

items.en: Odde is recorded meaning 'constituting a unit in excess of an even number', the arithmetic sense that English still keeps.
items.cn: odde 记录为“构成超出偶数的一个单位”，这是英语至今保留的算术义。

items.en: From Old Norse oddi 'third or additional number'. The same word also meant 'point of land, angle'.
items.cn: 来自古诺斯语 oddi“第三个数、额外的数”，同一个词还表示“土地的一角、尖角”。

items.en: Odda-maðr meant 'the third man, the one who breaks a tie', and odda-tala meant 'odd number', showing the 'extra unit' idea already at work.
items.cn: odda-maðr 指“第三个人、打破平票的人”，odda-tala 指“奇数”，说明“多余单位”的观念已在运作。

items.en: Oddi is related through oddr 'point of a weapon' to Proto-Germanic *uzdaz 'pointed upward', which also gives Old English ord 'spear point, beginning', German Ort 'place', and Lithuanian usnis 'thistle'. The link from 'point' to 'third number' is not found outside Norse and is source uncertain.
items.cn: oddi 经 oddr“武器尖端”与原始日耳曼语 *uzdaz“朝上的尖”相关，后者也给出古英语 ord“矛尖、起点”、德语 Ort“地点”和立陶宛语 usnis“蓟”。从“尖点”到“第三个数”这一步在诺斯语之外未见，来源不确定。

items.en: The sense 'strange, peculiar' is recorded from the 1580s, growing out of the idea of the one left out of the set; a favourable sense 'singular, remarkable' appears around 1400.
items.cn: “古怪、奇特”义自 16 世纪 80 年代有记录，由“被排除在套组之外的那一个”发展而来；约 1400 年已有“非凡、稀有”的褒义。

items.en: Modern English adds fixed phrases: odd job (1728), odd lot (1897), and the Odd Fellows society, a local club in the late 18th century and formally organised in 1813.
items.cn: 现代英语增添了固定说法：odd job（1728）、odd lot（1897），以及 Odd Fellows 互助会——18 世纪晚期为地方社团，1813 年正式组织。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: a poem addressed to a person or thing. It sounds the same as odd but comes from Greek oide 'song'.
entries.definitionCN: 献给某人或某物的颂诗。它与 odd 同音，但词源是希腊语 oide“歌”。

entries.definition: the plural of odd in its 'unequal remainder' sense: chances, or odds and ends. It is not a separate root word.
entries.definitionCN: odd 在“不相等余数”义上的复数：可能性、赔率或零碎杂物。它不是另一个词根词。

entries.definition: a strange person or thing. It is the noun built on odd with -ity.
entries.definitionCN: 怪人；怪事。它是由 odd 加 -ity 构成的名词。

entries.definition: unusual and hard to explain. It is the broad word, while odd often adds a touch of unease or mild humour.
entries.definitionCN: 不寻常且难以解释。它范围最广，odd 常多一层不安或轻微的调侃。

entries.definition: belonging to one person or thing in a way that stands out. It stresses distinctiveness, while odd stresses not fitting the set.
entries.definitionCN: 独特到显眼。它强调“专属、特别”，odd 强调“不合套组”。

entries.definition: unusual in a way that invites interest rather than unease. It is lighter and more neutral than odd.
entries.definitionCN: 奇特得引人好奇，而非令人不安。它比 odd 更轻、更中性。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Old Norse oddi 'third number', the odd one out, and the fixed phrases odd job, odds and ends and Odd Fellows.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：古诺斯语 oddi“第三个数”、the odd one out，以及固定说法 odd job、odds and ends、Odd Fellows。

normal.en: Old Norse oddi meant the third or additional number, the unit that breaks a tie in a vote.
normal.cn: 古诺斯语 oddi 指第三个数、额外的数，就是投票时打破平票的那一单位。

normal.en: A set works by pairs, so whatever cannot be paired is the odd one out.
normal.cn: 一套东西靠成对成立，配不上对的就是 the odd one out。

normal.en: Odd jobs are jobs that belong to no regular set; they are scattered and unpaired.
normal.cn: odd jobs 是不属于任何固定套组的活，零散而不成对。

normal.en: Odds and ends keeps the 'unequal remainder' idea: the scraps that no longer complete anything.
normal.cn: odds and ends 保留“不相等余数”的观念：再也凑不成完整东西的边角料。

normal.en: The arithmetic sense is the oldest: 1, 3, 5 are odd because one is always left over.
normal.cn: 算术义最古老：1、3、5 是奇数，因为每次都余下一个。

abstract.en: Picture three stones on a table: two can be paired, the third sits alone with a sharp corner showing.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上三块石头：两块能配上对，第三块孤零零待着，露出一个尖角。

abstract.en: The lone stone is arithmetic first, then a single glove, then a job that fits no schedule.
abstract.cn: 这块孤石先是算术，再是一只单手套，再是一份不合日程的零工。

abstract.en: When the lone stone is a person, the set's eyes turn on it, and 'left out' becomes 'strange'.
abstract.cn: 当孤石是一个人的时候，整套东西的目光都转向他，“落单”就变成了“古怪”。

examples.en: The street has odd numbers on one side and even numbers on the other.
examples.cn: 这条街一侧是奇数门牌，另一侧是偶数门牌。

examples.en: It seemed odd that such a careful man had left his bag on the train.
examples.cn: 这么细心的一个人竟把包落在火车上，显得很奇怪。

examples.en: She spent the afternoon sorting odds and ends in the bottom drawer.
examples.cn: 她花了一个下午整理最底层抽屉里的零碎东西。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥德」——奥德洗完衣服只剩一只袜子，又单又怪 → odd 单数的、落单的、古怪的

root: 源自约 1300 年的古诺斯语 oddi“第三个数、额外的数”，字面又指“土地的一角、尖角”，经 oddr“武器尖端”追到原始日耳曼语 *uzdaz“朝上的尖”；从“尖点”到“第三个数”这一步一般认为来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of odd all start from one picture: a unit that cannot be paired. That leftover then becomes an odd number, a single glove, a scattered job, a person set apart, a rough count, and finally the feeling of strangeness.
sensesIntro.cn: odd 的九个义项都从同一幅画出发：一个无法配对成双的单位。这个余数随后变成奇数、单只手套、零散活计、被排除在外的人、粗略的约数，最后变成“古怪”的感觉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one extra unit standing alone beside a matched pair.
core.cn: 核心意象：一对配好的东西旁边，多出一个独自站着的单位。

branches.en: THE NUMBER: the oldest branch, where one is always left over after pairing.
branches.cn: 数目：最古老的分支，两两配对后总会余下一。

branches.en: THE EXTRA UNIT: a single glove, a count a little past the round number, and the scraps that complete nothing.
branches.cn: 多出的单位：单只手套、略超整数的数目，以及凑不成任何东西的边角料。

branches.en: THE IRREGULAR: work and moments that belong to no fixed set and come only now and then.
branches.cn: 不规律：不属于固定套组、只是偶尔出现的工作与时刻。

branches.en: SET APART: the one a group cannot pair with, which draws attention, looks strange, and gives the Odd Fellows their name.
branches.cn: 被排除在外：群体配不上的那一个，它招来注意、显得古怪，也给 Odd Fellows 提供了名字。

branches.en: THE ODDs: unequal numbers turned into a measure of chance and betting.
branches.cn: 赔率：把不相等的数变成机会与赌博的量度。

intro.en: Odd is a bare Norse root with no living English prefix. English builds oddity with -ity and odds with the plural -s, and joins it into compounds such as oddball and odd-looking.
intro.cn: odd 是光秃的诺斯语词根，没有活的英语前缀。英语用 -ity 构成 oddity，用复数 -s 构成 odds，并把它并入 oddball、odd-looking 一类复合词。

latinIntro.en: Odd has no Latin source. Its recorded path is Old Norse oddi and, deeper, Proto-Germanic *uzdaz; the two entries below give those older forms rather than Latin words.
latinIntro.cn: odd 没有拉丁语来源。它的记录路径是古诺斯语 oddi，更深处是原始日耳曼语 *uzdaz；下面两条给出这些更早的形式，而不是拉丁词。

items.structure: odd (bare adjective from Old Norse oddi)
items.meaningCN: 奇数的；不成对的；零星的；古怪的

items.meaning: in a strange or unexpected way
items.meaningCN: 奇怪地；出乎意料地（-ly 构成副词）
items.exampleCN: 房间里安静得有些奇怪。

items.meaningCN: 奇怪；古怪（-ness 构成状态名词）
items.example: There was an oddness about the whole arrangement.
items.exampleCN: 整个安排透着一种古怪。

items.meaningCN: 怪人；怪事；古怪之处（-ity 构成名词）
items.example: The museum is full of mechanical oddities.
items.exampleCN: 博物馆里满是奇巧的机械装置。

items.example: Her oddball uncle kept a boat in the garden.
items.exampleCN: 她那古怪的叔叔在花园里放了一条船。

items.meaning: a leftover piece; a miscellaneous item
items.meaningCN: 零头；残余物；零星物品（-ment 构成名词）
items.example: A box of oddments sat on the shelf.
items.exampleCN: 架子上放着一盒零碎东西。

items.meaningCN: 可能性；赔率；零碎杂物（复数形式）
items.example: The odds of rain tomorrow are high.
items.exampleCN: 明天下雨的可能性很大。

items.meaningCN: 样子古怪的（复合形容词）
items.example: An odd-looking parcel arrived by post.
items.exampleCN: 一个样子古怪的包裹寄到了。

latinEntries.meaning: a third or additional number; point of land, angle
latinEntries.meaningCN: 第三个数、额外的数；土地的一角、尖角（古诺斯语）

definition_zh: 角；角度；视角；倾斜；钓鱼；鱼钩
definition_en: the space between two lines or surfaces that meet, the direction from which something is viewed, or, with a different origin, the act of fishing with a hook
core_image: 两条线从同一点分开，中间张开一个口
scene: 工匠把新做的搁板靠在墙边，抬头查看它与地面是否方正。 He checked the angle between the shelf and the wall with a small square tool.
sceneCN: 这里 angle 是「角、角度」（第 1 个义项：两条线或两个面相交形成的夹角）；句意为他用小角尺检查搁板与墙面之间的角度。画面里有靠墙的搁板、工匠与角尺。

pos.zh: 名词：角；角度；视角；倾斜；鱼钩（古旧义）
动词：钓鱼；斜行；从某一角度呈现

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 angulus 加 -ular 构成，义为「有角的；棱角分明的」
由 tri-「三」加 angle 构成，义为「三角形」
由 rect-「直」加 angle 构成，义为「长方形」
由钓鱼义的 angle 加 -er 构成，义为「钓鱼者」，这一支与几何义的 angle 词源不同

senses.title: The geometric angle
senses.definition: the figure formed by two lines or surfaces meeting at a point, measured in degrees
senses.definitionCN: 两条线或两个面在同一点相交所形成的图形，用度数计量
senses.example: A right angle measures exactly ninety degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 直角正好是九十度。
senses.why: Latin angulus meant a corner: the place where two edges meet is the original picture.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 angulus 意为「角、拐角」：两条边相交的那个地方就是最初的画面。

senses.title: A point of view
senses.definition: the direction or standpoint from which a situation is considered
senses.definitionCN: 看待某种情形时所采取的方向或立场
senses.example: From a different angle, the whole dispute looks much simpler.
senses.exampleCN: 换一个角度看，整场争执显得简单多了。
senses.why: If a corner is where you stand, then changing corners means changing how things look.
senses.whyCN: 如果「角」是你站的位置，那么换一个角，就等于换一种看事物的结果。

senses.title: A slant or tilt
senses.definition: a position that is not flat or upright but leaning away from the vertical
senses.definitionCN: 不是水平或垂直，而是偏离竖直方向的位置
senses.example: The old roof sits at a steep angle above the street.
senses.exampleCN: 旧屋顶以很陡的倾斜度压在街道上方。
senses.why: Two surfaces that are not square to each other leave a visible angle between them.
senses.whyCN: 两个面若不彼此方正，中间就会留下看得见的夹角。

senses.title: To fish with a hook
senses.definition: to fish, especially with a rod and hook; also used figuratively for trying to obtain something
senses.definitionCN: 钓鱼，尤指用竿与钩；也比喻设法获取某物
senses.example: He angled for trout in the cold stream all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 他一上午都在冰冷的溪流里钓鳟鱼。
senses.why: This sense comes from a different word, Old English angel 'fishhook', and only shares the modern spelling.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项来自另一个词，古英语 angel「鱼钩」，只是与几何义的 angle 共用今天的拼写。

senses.title: A fishhook
senses.definition: the older noun for a fishhook, now mainly historical
senses.definitionCN: 较古老的「鱼钩」名词义，今天主要出现在历史语境
senses.example: The fisherman lost his angle on a sunken branch.
senses.exampleCN: 渔夫的鱼钩挂在一根沉在水下的树枝上，丢了。
senses.why: Before the geometry word crowded it out, angle named the hooked tool itself.
senses.whyCN: 在几何义把这个词占满之前，angle 指的就是那个带钩的工具本身。

senses.title: A corner or street corner
senses.definition: an older use for a corner of a building or the meeting point of two streets
senses.definitionCN: 较旧的用法，指建筑的拐角或两条街道相交处
senses.example: They met at the angle of the two streets.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在两条街相交的拐角处见面。
senses.why: This keeps the Latin corner sense in its most literal, physical form.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁语「拐角」义最字面、最具体的保留。

intro.en: Angle is two different words that became one spelling: a Latin corner word and an Old English hook word.
intro.cn: angle 其实是两个不同的词合并成同一个拼写：一个来自拉丁语的「拐角」，一个来自古英语的「鱼钩」。

items.en: Angulus meant 'a corner, an angle'. It is the source of the geometric family and has no connection with fishhooks.
items.cn: angulus 意为「拐角、角」，是几何这一族的来源，与鱼钩毫无关系。

items.en: A separate word, angel, meant 'fishhook'. It belongs to a different root meaning 'hook, bend'.
items.cn: 另一个独立的词 angel 意为「鱼钩」，属于表示「钩、弯」的不同词根。

items.en: The geometric sense enters English through French, and angle begins to name corners and the space between meeting lines.
items.cn: 几何义经法语进入英语，angle 开始指拐角以及相交线之间的空间。

items.en: The fishing verb and noun continue alongside the geometric word, and the two spellings merge.
items.cn: 钓鱼的动词与名词与几何词并行发展，两者的拼写最终合一。

items.en: Geometry keeps angle and angular, while fishing keeps angler; the shared spelling hides two separate histories.
items.cn: 几何保留 angle 与 angular，钓鱼保留 angler；共同的拼写掩盖了两条彼此独立的历史。

note.en: The look-alike group mixes the corner family with the fishing word; the near-meaning group gathers corners and standpoints.
note.cn: 形近组把「拐角」一族与钓鱼词放在一起；近义组收拐角与立场类词。

entries.definition: Having angles or sharp corners; from Latin angulus.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有角的、棱角分明的」，来自拉丁语 angulus。

entries.definition: A flat shape with three straight sides, literally three angles.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「三角形」，字面就是「三个角」。

entries.definition: A four-sided shape with right angles, literally a right angle shape.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「长方形」，字面是「直角形」。

entries.definition: A person who fishes with a hook; this word comes from the Old English fishhook root, not from angulus.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「钓鱼者」，来自古英语「鱼钩」词根，并非来自拉丁语 angulus。

entries.definition: The point where two edges or streets meet; the plain everyday word for the Latin sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「角、拐角」，是拉丁语「角」义最日常的说法。

entries.definition: A way of looking at a matter, closer to the figurative angle.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「观点、立场」，接近 angle 的比喻义。

entries.definition: A particular way of judging things based on one's position or experience.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「视角、看法」，指基于位置或经验形成的判断方式。

entries.definition: A curve or turn in a road or line, not a measured angle.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「弯曲、转弯」，指道路或线条的转向，不是可度量的角。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the two real origins apart and attach them to the families they actually produced.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把两个真实来源分开，并各自挂到它们实际产生的词族上。

normal.en: Angulus is a corner: two edges meet and leave a measurable opening.
normal.cn: angulus 是「拐角」：两条边相交，留下一个可度量的开口。

normal.en: Old English angel is a fishhook: a different word that happens to share the modern spelling.
normal.cn: 古英语 angel 是「鱼钩」：另一个词，只是碰巧与今天的拼写相同。

normal.en: Triangle and rectangle are literally three-angle and right-angle shapes.
normal.cn: triangle 与 rectangle 字面就是「三个角」与「直角」的形状。

normal.en: Angler belongs to fishing, not geometry; its -er marks the person, not the corner.
normal.cn: angler 属于钓鱼而不是几何；它的 -er 标出的是人，不是角。

normal.en: From a different angle is the fixed phrase for a change of standpoint.
normal.cn: from a different angle 是表示「换立场」的固定说法。

abstract.en: Picture two roads leaving one crossroads, the space between them opening wider as they go.
abstract.cn: 想象两条路从同一个十字路口分开，越走中间的空隙越大。

abstract.en: Picture a camera moved one step to the side: the same room, a different story.
abstract.cn: 想象摄影机往旁边挪了一步：同一个房间，讲出了不同的故事。

abstract.en: Picture a hook under water, curved like a bent corner, waiting for a pull.
abstract.cn: 想象水下一只钩子，弯得像一个折角，等着被拉动。

examples.en: He checked the angle between the shelf and the wall with a small square tool.
examples.cn: 他用小角尺检查搁板与墙面之间的角度。

examples.en: From a different angle, the whole dispute looks much simpler.
examples.cn: 换一个角度看，整场争执显得简单多了。

examples.en: He angled for trout in the cold stream all morning.
examples.cn: 他一上午都在冰冷的溪流里钓鳟鱼。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺够」——俺够了够墙角那个角度，又拿钩子去钓鱼：角、钓鱼

root: 几何义来自拉丁语 angulus「拐角、角」，经法语进入英语；钓鱼义来自古英语 angel「鱼钩」，属于表示「钩、弯」的另一词根。两词在现代英语中拼写合一，但历史彼此独立，不能混为一条词源。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses divide into two histories: four belong to the corner word, including the figurative standpoint, and two belong to the fishhook word.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项分成两条历史：四个属于「拐角」词，包括比喻的立场义；两个属于「鱼钩」词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two lines leave one point and open a measurable gap between them.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条线从同一点出发，中间张开一个可度量的口。

definition_zh: 欠（钱）；归功于；应给予；理应
definition_en: to have money still to pay, to be grateful to someone or something for a result, or to be under an obligation to give something
core_image: 账本上一行没有划掉的数字，提醒你还欠着别人
scene: 月底的餐桌上，一张写满数字的账单被推到对方面前。 I still owe you two hundred yuan for the tickets.
sceneCN: 这里 owe 是「欠钱」（第 1 个义项：还欠着钱没付）；句意为我还欠你买票的两百块钱。图中可辨识物件：账单、餐盘、被推到桌对面的手势。

derivatives.zh: 由 owe 加 -ing 构成，表示「欠着的、尚未支付的」，常见于 owing to 表示「由于」
