senses.title: To have a debt to pay
senses.definition: to have borrowed money or goods and not yet paid for them
senses.definitionCN: 借了钱或拿了东西，还没有付清
senses.example: I still owe the shop twenty pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 我还欠那家店二十英镑。
senses.why: The Old English verb āgan meant to possess; a debt is what another person still holds a claim on, so the word came to name the part not yet handed over.
senses.whyCN: 古英语动词 āgan 本义是拥有；债务正是别人仍握有权利的那部分，于是这个词转指你还没交还出去的东西。

senses.title: To be grateful for a result
senses.definition: to be grateful to a person or thing because they made a good result possible
senses.definitionCN: 因为某人或某物促成了好结果而感激他
senses.example: She owes her career to a teacher who believed in her.
senses.exampleCN: 她把事业归功于一位相信她的老师。
senses.why: If a person still holds what you received, the debt can be a debt of gratitude; the ledger moves from money to credit for a result.
senses.whyCN: 如果一个人仍握着你得到的好处，这份债就成了感激之债；账本从金钱转成了对某份成果的功劳记录。

senses.title: To be under an obligation to give
senses.definition: to be obliged to give someone something such as an apology, an explanation or attention
senses.definitionCN: 有义务给某人某样东西，如道歉、解释或关注
senses.example: You owe him an explanation for leaving so suddenly.
senses.exampleCN: 你突然离开，欠他一个解释。
senses.why: A debt need not be money: any unfinished obligation, from an apology to a phone call, sits in the same place on the ledger.
senses.whyCN: 债不一定是钱：任何没完成的义务，从一句道歉到一个电话，都记在账本的同一栏。

senses.title: To be morally required to do something
senses.definition: in the phrase owe it to someone, to be morally required to do something for that person, especially for oneself
senses.definitionCN: 在 owe it to someone 这一说法里，指道义上应该为某人做某事，尤其应为自己的利益去做
senses.example: You owe it to yourself to take a real holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 你理应给自己放一个真正意义上的假。
senses.why: The same ledger can record a duty owed to oneself, which is why the phrase turns a moral claim into a kind of unpaid account.
senses.whyCN: 同一本账也能记下一个人对自己的责任，所以这个说法把道义要求写成了一笔尚未付清的账。

intro.en: Owe goes back to Old English āgan, to have or to possess; its modern meaning of debt grew out of the idea of something still held by another party.
intro.cn: owe 源自表示「拥有、持有」的古英语 āgan；今天「欠」的意思，是从「东西仍被另一方握有」这一观念长出来的。

items.en: The verb āgan meant to own, to have and to hold; a person could āgan land, cattle or money.
items.cn: 动词 āgan 意为拥有、持有；人可以拥有土地、牲畜或钱财。

items.en: A past form āhte began to take the sense of having a claim upon someone, and this is the seed of the debt sense.
items.cn: 过去式 āhte 开始带有「对某人拥有权利」的意思，这就是债务义的种子。

items.en: Middle English owen already meant both to possess and to be obliged to pay, depending on the sentence.
items.cn: 中古英语的 owen 已同时表示「拥有」与「有义务支付」，要看句子而定。

items.en: As own took over the plain sense of possession, owe was left with debt and obligation, and the split became permanent.
items.cn: 随着 own 接掌了纯粹的「拥有」义，owe 只剩下债务与义务，这一分工最终固定下来。

items.en: Modern English keeps owed and owing, and the phrase owing to, where a debt becomes the reason for something.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 owed 与 owing，以及 owing to，在那里一笔债变成了某事的原因。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the old verb of holding and its surviving relatives; the near-meaning group follows debt, gratitude and its opposite, repayment.
note.cn: 形近组沿着表示「持有」的旧动词及仍在使用的亲属词展开；近义组沿着债务、感激以及它的另一面——偿还——展开。

entries.definition: To possess something as property; the two words split from the same Old English verb.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有某物；这两个词由同一个古英语动词分出。

entries.definition: The old past tense of owe, now a modal verb for duty.
entries.definitionCN: owe 历史上的过去式，今为表示义务的情态动词。

entries.definition: Still unpaid, or, in owing to, because of.
entries.definitionCN: 尚未支付的；在 owing to 中表示「由于」。

entries.definition: Owing money, or grateful for help received.
To say that something is caused by a particular person or thing.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事归因于某人或某物。

entries.definition: To give someone praise for an achievement.
To pay back money that was borrowed.

normalIntro.en: The word is an old verb of holding whose debt sense survived while own took the plain sense of possession.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词原本是表示「持有」的旧动词，债务义留了下来，而纯粹的「拥有」义交给了 own。

normal.en: The Old English verb meant to have; a debt is what another person still has over you.
normal.cn: 古英语动词本义是持有；债务就是别人仍对你持有的一份东西。

normal.en: Own and owe split from the same verb: own keeps the possession, owe keeps the obligation.
normal.cn: own 与 owe 由同一个动词分出：own 留下拥有，owe 留下义务。

normal.en: Owing to works like a note on a receipt: one thing is charged to the account of another.
normal.cn: owing to 像收据上的备注：一件事被记到另一件事的账上。

normal.en: Ought is the old past tense of owe, which is why both still deal with duty.
normal.cn: ought 是 owe 旧的过去式，所以两者至今都在谈「应当」。

normal.en: You can owe an apology as easily as money; both are entries not yet settled.
normal.cn: 道歉和钱一样可以欠；两者都是还没结清的一笔。

abstract.en: A debt is a thread that keeps two people connected until it is paid.
abstract.cn: 债是一根线，在付清之前把两个人连着。

abstract.en: Gratitude is a ledger with no money in it, only names.
abstract.cn: 感激是一本没有钱数、只有名字的账。

abstract.en: To owe is to admit that part of what you are came from somewhere else.
abstract.cn: 欠，就是承认你之所以成为现在的样子，有一部分来自别处。

examples.en: I still owe the shop twenty pounds.
examples.cn: 我还欠那家店二十英镑。

examples.en: She owes her career to a teacher who believed in her.
examples.cn: 她把事业归功于一位相信她的老师。

examples.en: You owe him an explanation for leaving so suddenly.
examples.cn: 你突然离开，欠他一个解释。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧」——欠债的人看到账单只会喊一声「欧」，记住 owe 是欠。

root: 古英语 āgan（拥有、持有）到中古英语 owen；拥有义后来交给 own，owe 专指欠与归功于。同族词还有 ought、owing。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an unsettled claim; the senses spread from money to gratitude, to social obligations, and finally to duties owed to oneself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一笔没结清的权利；义项从金钱扩展到感激、社交义务，最后落到对自己也欠着一份责任。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line in a notebook that has not been crossed out.
core.cn: 核心意象：本子上那一行始终没有划掉的记录。

branches.en: a shopkeeper's notebook with an unpaid line
branches.cn: 店主本子上没划掉的一行

branches.en: a teacher named in a speech of thanks
branches.cn: 致谢演讲里被点名的老师

branches.en: an unsent apology waiting on a phone screen
branches.cn: 手机屏幕上一条没发出的道歉

branches.en: a tired worker finally booking a holiday
branches.cn: 疲惫的职员终于订下了假期

branches.en: a debt to another person and a debt to oneself
branches.cn: 欠别人的一笔，欠自己的一笔

intro.en: The forms come from one Old English verb of holding, with an old past tense that survives as a modal verb and an -ing form that still marks an unpaid sum.
intro.cn: 这些形式都出自同一个表示「持有」的古英语动词，其中一个旧过去式作为情态动词留存，一个 -ing 形式仍表示未付的款项。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; it descends from an Old English verb of holding.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；它出自一个表示「持有」的古英语动词。

items.meaningCN: owe 的过去式与过去分词

items.meaning: should, from the old past of owe
items.meaningCN: 应当，源自 owe 的旧过去式

definition_zh: 定期地；经常地；按规律地；均匀地；正式地
definition_en: again and again at even intervals, in a steady pattern, or in the usual proper way
core_image: 节拍器不间断地摆动：每一次摆动都落在同一个刻度上，从不迟到也从不抢拍
scene: 小区里那位老人每天六点整出现在湖边，风雪无阻，四十年了。 He visits the lake library regularly to read the newspapers.
sceneCN: 这里 regularly 是「定期地；经常地」（第 1 个义项：按均匀间隔反复发生）；句意：他定期去湖畔图书馆读报。场景要点：清晨的湖、固定的座位、翻旧了的报纸。

pos.zh: 定期地；经常地；按规律地；均匀地；正式地

derivatives.zh: 同根形容词，义为「规律的；定期的；常规的」
加否定前缀构成，义为「不规则地；不定期地」
同根名词，义为「规律性；均匀」
同根动词，义为「管理；调节」

senses.title: Again and again at even intervals
senses.definition: happening again and again with the same amount of time between each occasion
senses.definitionCN: 反复发生，且每次之间间隔的时间相等
senses.example: The committee meets regularly on the first Monday of each month.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会每月第一个周一定期开会。
senses.why: The bar of regula touches time at equal marks: each event lands on the same tick.
senses.whyCN: regula 的直杆以相等的刻度触及时间：每个事件都落在同一格上。

senses.title: In a steady, even pattern
senses.definition: in a way that has an even pattern, spacing, or rhythm, without irregularity
senses.definitionCN: 以均匀的样式、间距或节奏进行，毫无凌乱
senses.example: The regularly spaced windows give the tower its calm look.
senses.exampleCN: 间距均匀的窗户赋予塔楼沉静的气质。
senses.why: The bar is laid over space here: every window sits on the same line.
senses.whyCN: 这里直杆量的是空间：每扇窗都落在同一条线上。

senses.title: Often, as a settled habit
senses.definition: often, as part of an established habit or programme
senses.definitionCN: 频繁地，作为已确立的习惯或安排的一部分
senses.example: He regularly forgets his umbrella, and regularly complains about it.
senses.exampleCN: 他经常忘带伞，也经常为此抱怨。
senses.why: The even marks become habit when they are kept again and again: the tick turns into a trait.
senses.whyCN: 均匀的刻度被一次次遵守便成了习惯：钟摆的一格变成了性格的一笔。

senses.title: In the normal proper way
senses.definition: in the usual, correct, or officially proper manner
senses.definitionCN: 以通常、正确或官方正当的方式进行
senses.example: The goods were regularly imported, with all duties paid.
senses.exampleCN: 货物是正规进口的，关税全数缴清。
senses.why: The bar approves what passes over it: passing the measure is being regular.
senses.whyCN: 直杆核准从它上面通过之物：通过量度即是正规。

intro.en: Regularly is the adverb of regular, from Latin regularis, from regula 'a straight bar, a rule', from regere 'to keep straight, guide'. The suffix -ly turns the bar's measure into a manner of happening.
intro.cn: regularly 是 regular 的副词形式，regular 出自拉丁语 regularis，上溯 regula「直杆、规则」，regula 又出自 regere「保持笔直、引导」。后缀 -ly 把直杆的量度变成事情发生的方式。

items.en: The root *h3reg- 'to straighten, direct' underlies regere and its English cousins right, reckon and rich.
items.cn: 词根 *h3reg-「拉直、引导」是 regere 的来源；英语 right、reckon、rich 与之同根。

items.en: Regula named the carpenter's straight edge and any rule; regularis meant 'according to the rule'. The adverb could not exist in Latin; manner had to be said with phrases.
items.cn: regula 指木匠的直尺及一切规则；regularis 意为「依规而行」。拉丁语没有现成副词，方式须用短语表达。

items.era: OLD FRENCH AND MIDDLE ENGLISH, 14TH C.
items.en: Reguler enters English as the adjective; the adverb regularly appears soon after, built with the native -ly ending.
items.cn: reguler 以形容词身份进入英语；副词 regularly 随即出现，配上了本土的 -ly 词尾。

items.en: The adverb spreads from religious observance to clocks, trains, publishing and medicine: whatever repeats can be said to happen regularly.
items.cn: 副词从宗教操守扩散到钟表、铁路、出版与医学：凡重复之事皆可言 regularly。

items.en: The phrase exercise regularly fixed the health sense, and the ironic use of regularly for annoying habits gives it a light conversational tone.
items.cn: exercise regularly 确立了健康义；regularly 反讽地用于恼人的习惯，让它带上轻松的会话语气。

note.en: The first group gathers the regula family and its negation. The second group compares the adverbs of repetition and steadiness.
note.cn: 第一组汇集 regula 词族及其否定形式。第二组比较「重复」与「稳定」两类副词。

entries.definition: even and rule-keeping, said of things and people. It is the adjective the adverb leans on.
entries.definitionCN: 规律的；常客。是副词所依托的形容词。

entries.definition: at uneven intervals or in an unlawful way. The bar finds nothing even.
entries.definitionCN: 不规则地；非正式地。直杆量不出均匀。

entries.definition: an official rule. When something is done regularly by law, a regulation stands behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 规章。凡依法定期进行之事，背后必有一条 regulation。

entries.definition: a system of rule or a planned routine. The bar held as reins.
entries.definitionCN: 政权；体制；训练方案。直杆被当作缰绳握着。

entries.definition: to keep something even by rule. The verb that makes the adverb true.
entries.definitionCN: 用规则管制。让这个副词成立的动词。

entries.definition: at fixed periods. It names the clock's cycle; regularly names the evenness kept within it.
entries.definitionCN: 周期性地。periodically 命名时钟的周期；regularly 命名其中保持的均匀。

entries.definition: often, without implying even spacing. Frequently counts visits; regularly measures them.
entries.definitionCN: 频繁地，不含间隔均匀之意。frequently 数次数；regularly 量间隔。

entries.definition: by settled habit. It points inward to the person's pattern; regularly points to the outside clock.
entries.definitionCN: 习惯性地。habitually 指向人的内在模式；regularly 指向外在的钟摆。

entries.definition: all the time, without stopping. Constantly removes the gaps; regularly measures them.
entries.definitionCN: 持续不断地。constantly 消除了间隔；regularly 量着间隔。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin regula 'a straight bar' from regere 'to keep straight', the suffix -ly for manner, the family irregularly, regulation and regulate.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 regula「直杆」（出自 regere「保持笔直」），方式副词后缀 -ly，词族 irregularly、regulation、regulate。

normal.en: Regular plus -ly: the bar's even measure turned into a way of happening.
normal.cn: regular 加 -ly：直杆的均匀量度变成了事情发生的方式。

normal.en: The -ly ending is the native English way to make adverbs, as in quick, quickly.
normal.cn: -ly 是英语本土的副词后缀，如 quick 变 quickly。

normal.en: Irregularly simply denies the even marks: the ticks fall where they like.
normal.cn: irregularly 只是否定均匀的刻度：钟点随心所欲地落。

normal.en: Regularly scheduled means the timetable was set by the invisible bar.
normal.cn: regularly scheduled 意为时刻表由那根看不见的直杆排定。

normal.en: He regularly forgets his umbrella: even his mistakes keep perfect time.
normal.cn: 他经常忘带伞：连他的失误都守着准点。

abstract.en: Picture rain falling on a drum skin, each drop landing exactly one second after the last.
abstract.cn: 想象雨点落在鼓面上，每一滴都恰好比上一滴晚一秒。

abstract.en: Regularity is the quietest kind of beauty: nothing deviates, so the eye can rest.
abstract.cn: 规律是最安静的美：没有任何偏离，眼睛得以休息。

abstract.en: A habit is a clock you build inside yourself and then obey.
abstract.cn: 习惯是你装在自己体内的钟，装好之后还得服从它。

examples.en: She writes to her old teacher regularly, twice a month.
examples.cn: 她定期给老教师写信，每月两封。

examples.en: The lamps are cleaned regularly to keep the street bright.
examples.cn: 路灯定期清洁，以保持街道明亮。

examples.en: The pills must be taken regularly, not just when you feel ill.
examples.cn: 药必须按时服用，不能只在难受时才吃。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞古乐利」——瑞福古板却有「利」于健康：定期锻炼，从不间断 → regularly 定期地；经常地（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 regula「直杆；规则」（regere 引直）加副词后缀 -ly，核心是「按直杆的均匀刻度反复发生」。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of regularly, one even tick applied to time, to space, to habit, and to law.
sensesIntro.cn: regularly 的四个义项是同一声均匀的钟摆，分别作用于时间、空间、习惯与法律。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tick that always lands on the same mark, in time or in space.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个总是落在同一刻度上的钟点，无论在时间还是空间里。

branches.en: TIME AND HABIT: even intervals kept long enough become a person's routine.
branches.cn: 时间与习惯：均匀间隔被长期遵守，便化作一个人的日常。

branches.en: SPACE: the same evenness laid over windows, teeth and lamps.
branches.cn: 空间：同样的均匀铺在窗户、齿轮与路灯上。

branches.en: LAW: what the rule approves is done regularly, in the proper way.
branches.cn: 法律：经规则核准之事，即为正规地进行。

branches.en: ONE BAR, TWO DIMENSIONS: the straight edge measures both the clock and the wall.
branches.cn: 一杆两用：同一根直尺既量时钟，也量墙壁。

branches.en: INSIDE AND OUTSIDE: the settled habit is personal; the proper manner is official.
branches.cn: 内与外：固定的习惯属于个人；正当的方式属于官方。

intro.en: Regularly builds on regular with the native adverb suffix -ly; regular itself is regula 'a straight bar' with the Latin adjective ending. The negated form irregularly uses the shifted prefix ir-.
intro.cn: regularly 由 regular 加本土副词后缀 -ly 构成；regular 本身是 regula「直杆」加拉丁形容词词尾。否定形式 irregularly 使用音变后的前缀 ir-。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is regularis 'according to the regula', the carpenter's straight bar that became the very idea of a rule. Regere 'to keep straight' is the verb behind the bar.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语源头是 regularis「依 regula 而行」，regula 是木匠的直尺，后来成为「规则」观念本身。直尺背后的动词是 regere「保持笔直」。

items.meaning: at even intervals; as a habit; properly
items.meaningCN: 定期地；经常地；正规地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: Water the plants regularly in summer.
items.exampleCN: 夏天要定期给植物浇水。

items.meaning: even, by rule; a habitual visitor
items.meaningCN: 规律的；常客（-ar 构成形容词）
items.example: He is a regular volunteer here.
items.exampleCN: 他是这里的固定志愿者。

items.meaningCN: 不规则地；不定时地（ir- 表否定）
items.example: The buses run irregularly on holidays.
items.exampleCN: 节假日公交车班次不定。

items.meaningCN: 规律性；均匀（-ity 构成性质名词）
items.example: The regularity of the tides aids navigation.

items.meaningCN: 调节；管制（-ate 构成动词）
items.example: A thermostat regulates the room temperature.
Wear goggles: that is a site regulation.
items.exampleCN: 戴护目镜，这是工地规章。

items.meaningCN: 周期性地（出自希腊语 periodos「环绕一周」，与 regularly 词源不同）
items.exampleCN: 系统在夜间周期性更新。

items.meaningCN: 通常（出自拉丁 usus「使用」，与 regularly 词源不同）
items.example: The shop usually opens at eight.

items.meaningCN: 一般地；总体上（出自拉丁 genus「种类」）
稳定地（拉丁 stabilis「牢固的」）
items.example: Prices have remained stably low this year.
items.exampleCN: 今年物价稳定保持在低位。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 依规而行的；合乎规则的

definition_zh: 处罚；罚款；刑罚；（体育）点球、罚球；罚杆；不利后果；代价
definition_en: a punishment or disadvantage imposed for breaking a rule, failing a standard, or gaining an unfair advantage
core_image: 裁判在记分牌上划掉犯规一方的一分，再让对方站到更有利的位置上
scene: 足球场上，后卫在禁区里从背后绊倒对方前锋，裁判指向点球点，并向犯规者出示黄牌。 The referee awarded a penalty after the defender tripped the striker inside the box.
sceneCN: 这里指「体育比赛中因犯规而判给对方的一次罚球」，对应第 4 个义项：犯规之后由对方在固定位置主罚的一脚；句意为后卫在禁区内绊倒前锋后，裁判判给了点球。画面要点：禁区线、点球点、裁判手中的黄牌；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 处罚；罚款；刑罚（可数，常与 impose、pay、face 连用）
（体育）点球、罚球；罚杆（可数，足球、橄榄球、高尔夫常用）

derivatives.zh: 与 penalty 同出拉丁 poena，经形容词 poenalis 进入英语 → 由「那笔罚」转为形容「与刑罚有关的性质」
由 penal 加动词后缀（经法语与拉丁语，表「使……化」）→ 语义由「属于刑罚的」转为「施加处罚这一动作」
由 penalize 加名词后缀（源自拉丁语，表动作或结果）→ 由「施加处罚」转为「被处罚的过程或状态」
penalty 加复数后缀 → 由一次处罚转为多起、多类处罚
与 penalty 同出拉丁 poena，经动词 punire 加形容词后缀（源自拉丁语，表倾向）→ 由「罚金」转为「以惩罚为目的、带有惩罚性质的」

senses.title: A punishment for a breach
senses.titleCN: 因违反规则而受的处罚
senses.definition: a punishment imposed on a person or group that has broken a rule or failed a duty
senses.definitionCN: 对违反规则或未尽义务的个人与团体所施加的惩罚
senses.example: The league imposed a heavy penalty on the club for breaching the salary cap.
senses.exampleCN: 联盟因该俱乐部违反工资上限而对其处以重罚。
senses.why: Latin poena named the price exacted after a wrong, so the word begins as the consequence that follows a fault, not as the fault itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 poena 指犯错之后被索取的代价，所以这个词从一开始就是过错之后随之而来的后果，而不是过错本身。

senses.title: Money exacted for an offence
senses.titleCN: 为违法行为缴纳的钱款
senses.definition: a sum of money that an offender is required to pay to the authority that recorded the offence
senses.definitionCN: 违法者必须向记录该行为的机关缴纳的一笔钱
senses.example: Drivers face a penalty of two hundred pounds for using a phone at the wheel.
senses.exampleCN: 司机开车时使用手机，将面临两百英镑的罚款。
senses.why: Since poena also meant the compensation handed over to settle a wrong, the abstract consequence could be counted out in coins.
senses.whyCN: 因为 poena 也指为平息过错而交出的补偿，这种抽象的后果便可以用钱币数出来。

senses.title: A punishment fixed in statute
senses.definition: the punishment that a law prescribes for a particular offence, usually stated as a maximum
senses.definitionCN: 法律为某一具体罪行规定的惩罚，通常以最高刑期或最高数额表述
senses.example: The statute carries a maximum penalty of ten years in prison.
senses.exampleCN: 该法条规定的最高刑罚是十年监禁。
senses.why: When a community writes the price of a wrong into a code, the word shifts from the verdict spoken in court to the number printed in the law book.
senses.whyCN: 当共同体把过错的代价写进法典，这个词就从法庭上宣读的判决，转为法律文本里印着的那个数目。

senses.title: A free shot awarded for a foul
senses.titleCN: 因犯规而判给对方的罚球
senses.definition: an advantage given to the opposing side in a sport because the other side broke a rule
senses.definitionCN: 体育比赛中因一方犯规而判给另一方的有利机会
senses.example: The referee awarded a penalty after the defender tripped the striker inside the box.
senses.exampleCN: 后卫在禁区内绊倒前锋后，裁判判给了点球。
senses.why: Sport borrowed the legal word because a foul must be paid for; here the payment takes the form of an unopposed shot from a marked spot.
senses.whyCN: 体育借用了法律用词，因为犯规必须付出代价；在这里，代价的形式是在固定点上无人防守的一脚射门。

senses.title: A stroke added in golf
senses.titleCN: 高尔夫中被加罚的一杆
senses.definition: an extra stroke added to a player's score as a punishment for a mistake on the course
senses.definitionCN: 球场上因失误而被加进球员成绩里的一杆
senses.example: His ball found the water, so he took a penalty and dropped again.
senses.exampleCN: 他的球落进水里，于是他接受罚杆后重新抛球。
senses.why: Golf counts strokes instead of money, so paying for a mistake means adding a stroke to your own card.
senses.whyCN: 高尔夫数的是杆数而不是钱，所以为失误付出代价，就是在自己的记分卡上多加一杆。

senses.title: A charge for breaking a contract
senses.titleCN: 违反合同条款应付的违约金
senses.definition: an amount that a contract requires one party to pay if it acts in a way the agreement forbids
senses.definitionCN: 合同要求一方在做出协议禁止的行为时支付的款项
senses.example: Early repayment of the loan triggers a penalty of one month's interest.
senses.exampleCN: 提前偿还贷款会触发相当于一个月利息的违约金。
senses.why: A contract fixes in advance what a breach will cost, turning the older idea of compensation into a clause with a stated figure.
senses.whyCN: 合同事先定明违约要花多少钱，把较早的「补偿」观念变成一条写着具体数目的条款。

senses.title: The price of an advantage
senses.definition: a disadvantage that comes with a privilege or a success rather than with a rule broken
senses.definitionCN: 伴随特权或成功而来的不利之处，而不是因违规招致的
senses.example: Fame brought her the penalty of constant scrutiny.
senses.exampleCN: 名气给她带来了被人时刻审视的代价。
senses.why: If every gain carries a price, then even a privilege can carry a penalty, although no rule has been broken.
senses.whyCN: 如果每一种获得都带着价码，那么连特权也能带上「罚」，尽管并没有谁违规。

senses.title: A handicap laid on a contestant
senses.titleCN: 加在参赛者身上的不利条件
senses.definition: a disadvantage imposed on a competitor in order to equalize unequal starting points
senses.definitionCN: 为使不相等的起跑条件趋于平衡而加在某位参赛者身上的不利条件
senses.example: The older runners started with a time penalty.
senses.exampleCN: 年长的跑者带着时间上的不利条件起跑。
senses.why: Any contest that tries to balance unequal starting points can turn punishment into a handicap placed on the stronger side.
senses.whyCN: 凡是试图平衡起跑差距的比赛，都能把「罚」变成加在占优一方身上的不利条件。

intro.en: Penalty comes from Latin poena 'penalty, punishment, compensation', itself a loan from Greek poine 'price paid for a wrong'. Through Old French penalite it entered English law. Dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: penalty 出自拉丁语 poena「处罚、惩罚、补偿」，而 poena 又借自希腊语 poine「为过错付出的代价」；它经古法语 penalite 进入英语法律用语。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Poine named the price that settled a wrong, whether blood-money paid to a family or a fine owed to a community.
items.cn: poine 指为平息过错而付出的价，既可以是赔给家族的偿命钱，也可以是交给共同体的罚金。

items.en: Poena kept both halves of that idea: the punishment itself and the sum handed over in compensation.
items.cn: poena 保留了这个观念的两半：处罚本身，以及作为补偿交出的那笔钱。

items.en: The adjective poenalis 'of punishment' produced English penal and later supplied the stem for penalize.
items.cn: 形容词 poenalis 意为「与处罚有关的」，它生成英语的 penal，后来又提供了 penalize 的词干。

items.en: Legal French used penalite for the punishment attached to an offence, and Middle English took the word in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 法律法语用 penalite 指附在某一罪行上的处罚，中古英语在十五世纪吸收了这个词。

items.en: Penalty first named a punishment in law, then any sum exacted, then any disadvantage fixed by an agreement.
items.cn: penalty 最初指法律上的处罚，随后指任何被索取的钱款，再后来指协议定下的任何不利后果。

items.en: Nineteenth-century football rules turned the word into the name of the kick itself, and golf gave it the sense of an added stroke.
items.cn: 十九世纪的足球规则把这个词变成那脚罚球本身的名称，高尔夫又赋予它「加罚一杆」的意思。

note.en: The first group gathers words built on the same Latin stem plus one mere look-alike; the second group offers near alternatives for a punishment or a burden.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词干的词，外加一个只是长得像的词；第二组是「处罚或负担」这一意思的近义替代。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'of punishment'; it describes the legal character of a measure, not the measure itself.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「刑罚的」的形容词；它描述一项措施的惩罚性质，而不指这项措施本身。

entries.definition: The verb built on penal; it names the act of imposing what a penalty names as a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 由 penal 构成的动词；penalty 指那件被施加的罚，这个动词则指施加的动作。

entries.definition: Formed from Latin punire rather than directly from poena; it stresses the intention to punish.
entries.definitionCN: 由拉丁动词 punire 而非直接由 poena 构成；它强调「意在惩罚」这一层。

entries.definition: A small room where food is kept; it merely looks like penalty in spelling and is not related to it in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 存放食物的小房间；只是拼写与 penalty 相似，并非同源。

entries.definition: A sum paid as punishment for an offence; it covers the money sense but not the sporting or contractual ones.
entries.definitionCN: 因违法而缴纳的一笔钱；它只覆盖金钱义，不覆盖体育与合同义。

entries.definition: A penalty applied by an authority to enforce a rule; broader in politics and diplomacy, narrower in sport.
entries.definitionCN: 权威为执行规则而施加的处罚；在政治与外交中范围更广，在体育中范围更窄。

entries.definition: Something lost by rule because of a fault; it stresses what is taken away rather than what is imposed.
entries.definitionCN: 因过错而按规则失去的东西；它强调被拿走的东西，而不是被施加的东西。

entries.definition: A disadvantage placed on a stronger competitor; it matches the sporting sense but carries no blame.
entries.definitionCN: 加在较强竞争者身上的不利条件；与体育义相合，但不含责备。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin stem, the real derived words and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词干、真实的派生词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Poena is the Latin word for the price of a wrong; a penalty is that price written down.
normal.cn: poena 是拉丁语中「过错的代价」，penalty 就是把这笔代价写下来。

normal.en: The same family runs through penal, penalize and punitive, all keeping the idea of a price to be paid.
normal.cn: 同一词族贯穿 penal、penalize 与 punitive，都保留「要付代价」这一层。

normal.en: Fixed phrases lock the senses: death penalty, penalty kick, penalty clause.
normal.cn: 固定搭配锁定义项：死刑、点球、违约金条款。

normal.en: A penalty is always owed to someone: a referee, a court or a contract.
normal.cn: 罚总是欠着某一方的：裁判、法庭或合同。

normal.en: If no rule was broken and nothing is owed, there is no penalty.
normal.cn: 若无人违规、无所亏欠，就谈不上罚。

abstract.en: Picture a coin box beside a rulebook, and every broken rule drops a coin in.
abstract.cn: 想象规则手册旁放着一只钱箱，每破一条规则就投进一枚硬币。

abstract.en: Picture a runner made to stand two steps behind the line because he started too early.
abstract.cn: 想象一名跑者因为抢跑，被要求站到起跑线后两步。

abstract.en: Picture a hill of trophies with a small toll gate at the foot, charging every winner.
abstract.cn: 想象一座由奖杯堆成的山，山脚设着一道小收费站，向每位赢家收费。

examples.en: The court added a penalty for the delay in reporting the accident.
examples.cn: 法院因事故报告延误而加判了一笔处罚。

examples.en: A penalty shoot-out decided the final.
examples.cn: 点球决胜决定了决赛的归属。

examples.en: There is a penalty for paying the loan back early.
examples.cn: 提前还贷是要付违约金的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派人提」——你一犯规，就派人来提走一笔钱 → 罚款、处罚

root: 希腊 poine「为过错付出的价」→ 拉丁 poena「处罚、补偿」→ 拉丁形容词 poenalis → 古法语 penalite → 英语 penalty；同族词有 penal、penalize、punitive、punish。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses rest on one move: a wrong creates a debt, and the debt is collected. The collection may be a punishment, a sum of money, a statutory sentence, a shot at goal, a golf stroke, a contractual charge, the price of privilege, or a handicap in a race.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都立于同一个动作：过错生出一笔债，这笔债要被收回。收回的形式可以是一次处罚、一笔钱、一条法定刑、一脚罚球、一杆罚杆、一项合同收费、特权的代价，或比赛中的不利条件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a referee striking one point off the offender's side and moving the other side forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：裁判从犯规一方的记分上划掉一分，再把另一方往前挪。

branches.en: LEGAL CONSEQUENCE: a fault creates a debt that a verdict or a statute collects in the form of punishment.
branches.cn: 法律后果：过错生出一笔债，由判决或法典以处罚的形式把它收回。

branches.en: MONEY FORM: the debt is counted in coins, from a fine owed to a public authority to a charge written into a contract.
branches.cn: 金钱形式：这笔债用钱币计算，从欠公共机关的一笔罚金到写进合同的一项收费。

branches.en: SPORTING FORM: the payment becomes an uncontested shot at goal or an extra stroke on the card.
branches.cn: 体育形式：这笔代价变成一脚无人防守的射门，或记分卡上多加的一杆。

branches.en: VOLUNTARY PRICE: a privilege or a success brings its own burden, although no rule was broken.
branches.cn: 自愿的代价：特权或成功自带负担，尽管并没有人违规。

branches.en: EQUALIZING BURDEN: a contest lays a disadvantage on the stronger side to level the start.
branches.cn: 平衡的负担：比赛把不利条件加在占优一方，使起跑趋于齐平。

intro.en: Penalty is a noun from the poena family; its Latin adjective and its related verb branch into several English words about punishment.
intro.cn: penalty 是 poena 词族中的名词；它的拉丁形容词与相关动词分出了若干与惩罚有关的英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin poena and poenalis give penal, penalty and penalize, while Latin punire, built on poena, gives punish, punishment and punitive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 poena 与 poenalis 生出 penal、penalty 与 penalize；由 poena 构成的拉丁 punire 则生出 punish、punishment 与 punitive。

items.example: The stem carries the idea of a debt owed after a fault.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干带着「犯错之后欠下一笔债」的意思。

items.example: The new law raised the penalties for dumping waste.
items.exampleCN: 新法提高了倾倒废弃物的处罚。

items.example: The country still keeps a penal code.
items.exampleCN: 该国仍然保留着一部刑法典。
规则对逾期提交予以处罚。

items.meaning: the act or state of being punished
items.example: He objected to the penalization of small firms.
items.exampleCN: 他反对对小企业施加处罚。

items.example: The measure was more punitive than preventive.
items.exampleCN: 这项措施更偏向惩罚，而非预防。

items.meaning: to make someone suffer for a wrong
the suffering imposed for a wrong
items.meaningCN: 因过错而被施加的痛苦
items.example: The punishment was a month without pay.
Such conduct is punishable by law.
items.exampleCN: 这种行为依法应受处罚。

latinEntries.meaning: to punish; to exact a penalty

definition_en: relating to emotions; showing strong feelings easily; causing strong feelings
core_image: 心里的水面被风一吹，立刻泛起层层波纹
scene: 电影放到重逢那场，观众席里有人轻轻抽泣。 The final scene was deeply emotional.
sceneCN: 这里 emotional 是「令人动情的」（第 03 个义项：引起强烈情感）；句意是最后一场戏非常动人。

senses.title: Relating to emotions
senses.definition: connected with feelings rather than with pure reason
senses.definitionCN: 与感受有关，而不是与纯粹理性有关
senses.example: Children need emotional support as well as food.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子除了食物，也需要情感支持。
senses.why: The adjective simply adds -al to emotion, so it labels whatever belongs to the stirred inner life.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是在 emotion 后加 -al，用来标记属于「被搅动的内心生活」的一切。

senses.title: Easily moved to strong feeling
senses.definition: showing feelings openly or becoming upset easily
senses.definitionCN: 公开表露感受，或很容易被触动
senses.example: He became emotional when he spoke about his mother.
senses.exampleCN: 谈到母亲时他动情了。
senses.why: A person whose inner water is easily stirred is called emotional, so the adjective also describes a low threshold for feeling.
senses.whyCN: 内心水面容易被搅动的人就被称为 emotional，所以这个形容词也形容感受的门槛很低。

senses.title: Causing strong feelings
senses.definition: producing strong feelings in an audience or reader
senses.definitionCN: 在观众或读者心中激起强烈感受
senses.example: The final scene was deeply emotional.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一场戏非常动人。
senses.why: A scene can stir the viewer the way a hand stirs water, so the adjective turns from the feeler to the thing that makes others feel.
senses.whyCN: 一场戏能像手搅水一样搅动观众，于是这个形容词从「感受者」转向「让别人产生感受的事物」。

intro.en: Emotional is a native English formation from emotion plus the adjective ending -al.
intro.cn: emotional 是英语在 emotion 后加形容词词尾 -al 构成的本土派生词。

items.en: The ultimate verb meant to move out or stir up.
items.cn: 最终源头动词意为移出、激起。

items.en: The noun named a stirring of the mind.
items.cn: 名词指心绪被搅动。

items.en: English borrowed the noun in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个名词。

items.en: The adjective emotional was formed with -al.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，加 -al 构成形容词 emotional。

items.en: It now covers the emotional life, a person's temperament and moving works of art.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖情感生活、人的性情与动人的艺术作品。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the emotion family; the near-meaning group separates sentimental, moving and passionate.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 emotion 词族展开；近义组区分多愁善感、动人以及充满激情。

entries.definition: A strong feeling.

entries.definition: In a way connected with feelings.
Arousing feeling, often used of words.

entries.definition: Producing a strong feeling of sadness or sympathy.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「动人的」，强调引发怜惜或悲伤。

entries.definition: Filled with very strong feeling or belief.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「充满激情的」，强度更高。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from emotion plus -al, then let the adjective describe the feeling life, the person and the artwork.

normal.en: Emotion plus -al makes the adjective.

branches.cn: 感受者与成因：被感动的人与动人的场景。

intro.en: Emotional is emotion plus -al, an adjective ending meaning relating to.
intro.cn: emotional 是 emotion 加 -al，这个词尾表示「与……有关的」。

latinIntro.en: The -al ending came through French and Latin, while the root movere is recorded Latin.
latinIntro.cn: -al 词尾经法语与拉丁语进入英语，词根 movere 则是有记录的拉丁语。

items.exampleCN: 它出现在 emotion 里面。
